description: The Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) degree program is a full-time, four-year undergraduate business program. It provides an opportunity to develop business acumen and leadership skills in a challenging, yet supportive, student-centered environment. Ross BBAs get a comprehensive education that includes business fundamentals, liberal arts courses, a required international experience, and a capstone course in which they start and run a real business. First-year applicants may apply directly to Ross for preferred admission consideration. Students not admitted to Ross through preferred admission may apply to Ross as a transfer student from another U-M unit, such as LSA, at the end of their first year.

Actuaries are professionals who work in the insurance and financial services industries. Their work is to analyze the financial consequences of risk. They use mathematics, statistics, and financial theory to study uncertain future events. Actuarial mathematics is the body of mathematics that is used by these professionals. Traditionally, actuarial mathematics has dealt primarily with the mathematics of life insurance, health insurance, property and casualty insurance, pensions, and social insurance. More recently, actuarial mathematics has grown to include the study of financial risk in a much wider setting. Examples of this are the pricing of stock options and other financial derivatives, and the development of sophisticated investment strategies.

Aerospace Engineering is the branch of engineering that deals with the design, analysis, testing, and production of aircraft, spacecraft, and related systems. Our undergraduates develop a solid foundation in the fundamentals of aerodynamics and propulsion, structural mechanics and materials, and flight dynamics and control systems. The program culminates in a senior-level capstone design course that gives students the opportunity to work in teams to design a complete aerospace vehicle system, such as a passenger aircraft, helicopter, satellite, or interplanetary probe.
Accreditation status: The Aerospace Engineering undergraduate program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

Concentration name: ['African Studies', 'Afroamerican and African Diaspora Studies']
description: The Department of Afroamerican and African Studies (DAAS) at the University of Michigan provides a multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary program of study about the history, culture, and society of Africa and the African diaspora. With over twenty core faculty members who conduct research on the African continent, the Caribbean, Latin America, and the United States, DAAS offers students a wide range of courses and concentrations that analyze the economic, political, and cultural formations of the African diaspora. Our courses expose students to current debates and new fields of knowledge and prepare them for careers in education, social work, law, public policy, and many other fields.

Concentration name: ['Arab and Muslim American Studies', 'Asian/Pacific Islander American Studies', 'Digital Studies', 'Latina/o Studies', 'Native American Studies']
description: The American Culture (AC) major offers an interdisciplinary approach to the study of United States society and culture. You’ll examine the country from multiple perspectives, drawing on sources from literature, history, the arts, and the social sciences. The program emphasizes the multicultural diversity of the American experience, asking you to look at the country through the lenses of race, ethnicity, class, gender, and religion. You will explore America in the contexts of its global and transnational relationships as well as the impact of its domestic diversity.

Concentration name: ['Biological Anthropology', 'Archaeology', 'Sociocultural Anthropology', 'Linguistic Anthropology', 'General Anthropology']
description: Anthropology is the study of humankind from a broad comparative and historical perspective. The field is traditionally divided into four subfields: biological anthropology, archaeology, sociocultural anthropology, and linguistic anthropology. Because of its breadth, a major in anthropology is an excellent foundation for a liberal arts education and can be a bridge to many other disciplines in the humanities (e.g., history, classics), the social sciences (e.g., sociology, psychology), and the natural sciences (e.g., biology, geology, environmental science).

The BSE in Applied Physics is jointly administered by the Department of Physics and the College of Engineering. It is intended for students who want to apply the principles of physics to the development of new technology. Students can choose to concentrate in an area of engineering or pursue an interdisciplinary course of study. Applied Physics students take core courses in physics and mathematics, as well as a selection of engineering courses chosen to provide a solid foundation in the engineering discipline of their choice. They also receive training in the design of experiments and in the process of technological innovation. With its combination of a solid background in basic science and an introduction to engineering, the Applied Physics program is excellent preparation for graduate study in either physics or engineering.

The Applied Exercise Science (AES) undergraduate program prepares students to be leaders in a variety of fields related to health, fitness, and the prevention and treatment of chronic disease. AES provides a strong science-based academic background, comprehensive professional development, and practical hands-on experiences to enable students to excel in a variety of health-related careers, including physical therapy, occupational therapy, physician assistant, medicine, and corporate wellness/fitness.

The Applied Fitness and Conditioning major prepares students for careers in applied exercise physiology, strength and conditioning, corporate wellness, and for graduate study in a number of health- and fitness-related fields. The required coursework addresses the American College of Sports Medicine (ACSM) standards and prepares students for their nationally accredited certifications (e.g., certified personal trainer, certified exercise physiologist). Students also have the opportunity to take advanced coursework in athletic training, biomechanics, exercise physiology, motor control, and sport management.

In the applied statistics major, students learn to use statistical methods to solve real-world problems. They gain a deep understanding of statistical theory and the ability to apply that theory to data analysis in a variety of fields. Students learn to use statistical software to analyze data, and they learn to communicate their findings to a variety of audiences. The applied statistics major is a good choice for students who are interested in a career in data science, business analytics, or a related field.

The minor in Arab and Muslim American Studies provides students with a broad yet deep, critical, and nuanced understanding of Arab and Muslim American peoples, histories, and cultures. Coursework introduces students to the core concepts, theories, and debates in the field. Students can study the social construction of race and ethnicity, gender and sexuality, and religion; transnationalism and diaspora; civil rights and civil liberties; war and empire; and cultural and artistic productions. A capstone course will guide students in developing a research project related to the field of Arab and Muslim American Studies, and an engagement component of the minor offers an opportunity for a sustained and meaningful application of students’ knowledge in a setting outside of the classroom.

Concentration name: sub-major in Arabic Language and Literature for students in the Residential College
description: The Arabic Studies major combines intensive language training with the study of the literature, history, and culture of the Arab world. Advanced study focuses on the structure and history of Arabic language and literature, as well as on Arabo-Islamic history and civilization. Students have opportunities to study abroad. This major may be a good fit for students considering careers in international affairs, government, international business, and journalism. There is a sub-major in Arabic Language and Literature for students in the Residential College.

The Interdepartmental Program in Archaeology and History enables students to combine the study of archaeology with the study of history in a rigorous, interdisciplinary major. Students can create a course of study which explores a particular period, region, or theme from both historical and archaeological perspectives. In order to allow for this flexibility, the major requires students to complete a core curriculum and then create an individual concentration of four additional courses. This concentration must be approved by a major advisor. The major requires either one semester of excavation experience or a second methods course.

The Architectural Studies minor is for students interested in the interdisciplinary study of architecture, its history, theories, and its varied cultural contexts from a liberal arts perspective. Its curriculum includes a wide range of courses in architectural history, theory, design, and technology. Students select a combination of architectural studies courses that best suit their interests, which can include topics such as sustainability, urbanism, digital technologies, and more.

As an undergraduate architecture student at U-M, you’ll join a community of thinkers and makers who are passionate about the built environment. Our curriculum emphasizes individual exploration and creative speculation within a robust professional program. You'll gain a strong foundation in the art of making, as well as the historical, theoretical, and technical aspects of architecture. Our graduates are problem solvers and critical thinkers with the skills to address contemporary challenges through design. The undergraduate program consists of two two-year components: Pre-Architecture and Architecture. In your first two years, you’ll focus on liberal arts distribution requirements and studio art foundation courses. After a selective secondary admission process, successful candidates will matriculate to the architecture major. In your junior and senior years, you'll immerse yourself in a curriculum focused on the built environment.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science in Architecture is a pre-professional degree and is not accredited by NAAB. The Master of Architecture degree is NAAB-accredited.

description: The Stamps School of Art & Design undergraduate curriculum is an open structure that provides a balance between broad inquiry and focused learning. While all students receive a BFA in Art & Design, our curriculum allows students to concentrate in a specific area of interest and provides the latitude to take a wide range of courses both in Stamps and in other academic units across campus. All students take foundation courses to build a solid base for their creative work; sophomore review to reflect on their progress; junior review to look ahead toward a career in the arts; and a senior studio to cap their four years of study. With a wide range of elective courses in 2D, 3D, and 4D media to choose from, students will find that the program offers enough flexibility to chart their own path to an arts degree, while still receiving a well-rounded and structured education. Students develop their creative skills in their choice of media, exploring a range of topics that reflect their personal interests as well as larger social concerns. They learn to think critically about their own creative work, developing the ability to analyze, critique, and talk and write about their art and design work. Students in Art & Design also learn about the role of the creative arts in society and prepare for careers in which they can make a difference.
Accreditation status: The Penny W. Stamps School of Art & Design is a founding member of and accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art & Design (NASAD).

Concentration name: Honors Major in History of Art
description: History of Art is the academic study of the history of art, architecture, and visual culture. The department’s curriculum provides a sophisticated and challenging introduction to a wide range of fields in the history of art and material culture. The faculty are internationally-recognized scholars who are also deeply committed teachers and mentors. As a history of art major, you'll work closely with faculty, enjoy small classes, and become part of a strong intellectual and social community within the larger University. You'll gain a historical understanding of the artistic traditions of diverse cultures and an appreciation of their richness and variety. You’ll become a sophisticated viewer and interpreter of visual art and culture. You will also learn how to think critically, to analyze, and to write persuasively. You will be able to undertake independent research in a field of your choice, which may lead to an honors thesis.

The Arts and Ideas in the Humanities (AIH) major is an interdisciplinary program for students who want to study the arts and humanities within a broad cultural and historical framework. It resembles a traditional humanities major, but offers more flexibility in its course selection, and differs from a traditional major by its emphasis upon ideas and cultural movements over any one subject matter. As an AIH major, you might focus on a specific medium (such as painting, literature, music or drama) or a specific historical period (such as the Renaissance or the modern era). The major is designed to permit you a large degree of freedom in forming your curriculum from the many diverse course offerings in the RC Humanities Division and in LSA. You will get to work closely with your advisor to create a program of study that best serves your intellectual interests and goals.
Program name: Arts and Ideas in the Humanities

Concentration name: ['China', 'Japan', 'Korea', 'South Asia', 'Southeast Asia']
description: The Asian Studies major is an interdisciplinary program that allows students to focus on one of five sub-regions: China, Japan, Korea, South Asia, or Southeast Asia. Students choose courses from an approved list that spans over twenty departments, including ALC, History, Political Science, and Sociology, in order to gain in-depth knowledge of one of these regions. In addition to coursework focused on a particular country or region, majors must complete four terms of an Asian language.

The undergraduate program in Astronomy and Astrophysics is designed for students who are fascinated by the universe and want to understand the physical principles that govern its behavior. The undergraduate program is designed to provide students with a strong background in mathematics and physics, as well as specialized knowledge in astronomy and astrophysics. The major consists of two main components: a set of core courses that all majors must take, and a set of elective courses that allow students to specialize in a particular area of interest. The major also includes a research component, which can be satisfied by completing a senior thesis or by participating in a research project with a faculty member. The undergraduate major is excellent preparation for graduate study in astronomy and related fields, such as planetary science and astrophysics. It also provides a strong foundation for careers in a variety of fields, including education, science writing, and data science.

Concentration name: Advanced Automotive Powertrains, Advanced Automotive Systems and Design
description: The University of Michigan Master of Engineering in Automotive Engineering is an advanced professional degree program that is designed specifically for today’s engineering world. It is an interdisciplinary program that is at the intersection of mechanical, electrical, computer, and materials science engineering. This degree addresses the increasing complexity of the automobile as a system, and will provide you with the skills to become a leader in the automotive industry. It is offered on-campus in Ann Arbor, online, or as a global hybrid program.

The Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Behavioral and Biological Sciences is a 120 credit hour interdisciplinary program combining a solid background in natural sciences with concentrated study in psychology and anthropology or sociology. The degree program is specifically designed to prepare students for graduate programs in the health sciences (e.g., medicine, dentistry, physical therapy) and other related health fields. This curriculum prepares students for graduate work in these fields by ensuring all pre-requisite coursework is completed as a part of their academic plan. The curriculum is also designed to provide a broad understanding of the biological and social determinants of health and illness. The undergraduate advisor for this major can help students explore professional school options, including those in allopathic medicine, osteopathic medicine, physician assistant, dentistry, optometry, pharmacy, physical therapy, and veterinary medicine.

Biochemistry is the study of the chemistry of life. It provides the foundation for biotechnology and is a fundamental part of many fields in the health sciences. Biochemists study the structure and function of the molecules of life including proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, and carbohydrates. Students will explore how these molecules are synthesized and degraded in organisms and how these processes are regulated. Biochemists also study how organisms extract energy from their surroundings to carry out the processes necessary for life.

Biochemistry, the chemistry of life, is an exciting and rapidly expanding field of study. The curriculum focuses on the chemical processes of living cells and the structure-function relationships of biomolecules. Students will be prepared for a variety of careers including graduate programs in biochemistry or related fields, medical school, pharmacy, patent law, government and industry.

Concentration name: ['Biochemical Engineering', 'Bioelectrics and Neural Engineering', 'Biomaterials and Regenerative Medicine', 'Biomechanics', 'Biomedical Imaging and Ultrasonics', 'Biotechnology and Systems Biology', 'Medical Product Development']
description: Bioengineering is a growing discipline focused on the application of engineering principles to the fields of biology and medicine to create new medical devices, therapies, and diagnostic tools to improve human health. The undergraduate curriculum provides a strong foundation in engineering and the life sciences, preparing students for careers in the biomedical and health care industries as well as for further graduate studies and professional schools.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science in Engineering degree program in Biomedical Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description: This program provides a broad, comprehensive background in biology, from molecules and cells to organisms and ecosystems. LSA offers several other biology-related majors with different emphases, including Biochemistry; Biology, Health, and Society; Cell and Molecular Biology; Ecology, Evolution, and Biodiversity; Microbiology; Neuroscience; and Plant Biology.

Concentration name: ['Biology, Health, and Society', 'Ecology, Evolution, and Biodiversity', 'General Biology', 'Neuroscience', 'Plant Biology']
description: The study of living organisms and their relationships to the non-living world. Students can select to obtain a general background in biology or to specialize in a variety of sub-disciplines that mirror the research strengths of the department. An Honors degree is also offered. Biology majors are well-prepared to pursue graduate work in biological fields; for professional school in the health sciences; for careers in biotechnology, conservation, and environmental sciences; for teaching; and for many other pursuits.

The Biology, Health, and Society (BHS) major, offered by the College of Literature, Science, and the Arts, is designed for students interested in the life sciences and their application to a variety of human health issues. Combining a strong biological science foundation with a multidisciplinary approach, BHS examines the interconnectedness of human health, biology, and society. The BHS major provides an excellent foundation for a number of different professional and graduate school programs, including medicine, dentistry, public health, law, and social work. The BHS major can also lead to careers in business, health care administration, genetic counseling, public policy, and science journalism.

Concentration name: ['Biochemical Engineering', 'Bioelectrics and Neural Engineering', 'Biomechanics and Biotransport', 'Biomaterials and Regenerative Medicine']
description: Biomedical engineering is the newest engineering discipline, applying problem-solving skills to the medical and biological fields. It bridges the gap between engineering and medicine, combining the design and problem-solving skills of engineering with medical and biological sciences to advance health care treatment, including diagnosis, monitoring, and therapy. As a biomedical engineer, you might design medical instruments and devices, including artificial internal organs, replacements for body parts, and diagnostic machines. You might conduct research to understand the workings of the human body and how it responds to engineered materials or interventions. Or you could design processes for making pharmaceutical products or develop new ways to ensure product quality and safety.
Accreditation status: The undergraduate program in Biomedical Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description: Biomolecular science represents a modern approach to the study of the chemistry of life. Its goal is a complete understanding of life at the molecular level. It lies at the interface of chemistry and biology, with an emphasis on structure and function.

Biophysics is an interdisciplinary major program in which students are trained to apply the concepts and techniques of physics to the understanding of biological systems. The curriculum is intended to prepare students for graduate study in biophysics, molecular biology, and other related fields, for medical school, or for employment in the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries. The Biophysics Major provides an excellent foundation for any career in quantitative modern biology or medicine. For a full list of program requirements, please see the LSA Course Catalog. Students in Biophysics develop a core competency in mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology. They then build upon this with specialized classes that emphasize how the different disciplines come together to understand complex biological systems. The major culminates with a two-semester capstone research experience for all majors.

Biopsychology, Cognition, and Neuroscience (BCN) is an interdisciplinary major that allows you to concentrate your studies on the neural mechanisms that underlie behavior. In addition to gaining a deeper understanding of the natural science of psychology, you will also receive intensive training in the related fields of biology, chemistry, and mathematics. This major is excellent preparation for graduate training in a variety of fields, including those related to human health and medicine, neuroscience, biopsychology, cognitive science, and cognitive neuroscience.

Concentration name: Birth to Kindergarten Education
description: The Birth to Kindergarten (B-K) teacher education program prepares students to become effective, thoughtful, and compassionate educators of young children from birth through kindergarten. Students learn to enact teaching practices that support children as they grow and develop, to partner with families and communities in support of children’s learning, and to disrupt injustices in early childhood education. Graduates of the B-K program earn a Bachelor of Arts degree in Learning, Education, and Policy and are recommended for a Michigan Standard Teaching Certificate with a B-K endorsement. The B-K endorsement certifies graduates to teach in general and special education classrooms from birth through kindergarten.

The Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) curriculum, leading to the BBA degree, is a four-year program for students who wish to pursue a course of study in business. The first year of the BBA curriculum is taken in another school or college at the University of Michigan, usually the College of Literature, Science, and the Arts (LSA). The BBA program includes a rigorous core, a wide range of business electives, and a required number of non-business courses to provide students with the intellectual breadth necessary to build a successful career. Students can also customize their curriculum with a variety of focus areas and special programs.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB).

Concentration name: Business Analytics pathway
description: The Technology and Operations area has recently developed a new academic pathway in Business Analytics for BBA students. This pathway is intended for students who have strong quantitative interests and skills, and who are interested in pursuing a career in analytics, including the areas of marketing analytics, operations analytics, financial analytics, and human resource analytics. Students will learn how to extract insights from data, and how to use those insights to make better business decisions.

The Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) program at Michigan Ross is one of the top undergraduate business programs in the world. Our BBA curriculum is designed to give you a strong foundation in the liberal arts and key business principles while preparing you for a successful career after graduation. You’ll have access to world-renowned faculty, action-based learning, and a supportive community of peers to guide you along the way.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB).

description: The Cellular and Molecular Biomedical Science (CMBS) major is a joint major offered by the Department of Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology (MCDB) and the Department of Cell & Developmental Biology (CDB) in the Medical School. This major focuses on the intersection of cell biology, development, and the molecular basis of human disease. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in the molecular, cellular, and developmental processes that are the basis for human health and disease. The courses will explore the mechanisms that direct the differentiation and organization of cells and tissues and how these mechanisms are affected in various disease states including cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, diabetes, and cardiovascular diseases. The curriculum also prepares students for many different careers including research, medicine, and other health professions, biotechnology, science policy, and education.

Concentration name: Electrical Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Materials Science and Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Sustainable Engineering
description: The University of Michigan Chemical Engineering undergraduate program is designed to be flexible and customizable. The core curriculum ensures a solid foundation in engineering and chemical engineering fundamentals while a wide variety of elective options allow each student to tailor their degree to their interests. The undergraduate program is designed to develop the students’ abilities to apply scientific and engineering principles to the solution of problems, to exercise critical and creative judgment, to communicate their ideas, and to prepare for a lifetime of learning and professional leadership.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science in Engineering (Chemical Engineering) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

Concentration name: ACS Certified
description: Chemistry, the central science, is the study of matter and its transformations. It deals with the composition, structure, and properties of substances and the changes they undergo. Understanding chemistry is fundamental to understanding the world around us. Majors explore the core areas of analytical, inorganic, organic, and physical chemistry. The department offers three separate majors in chemistry, as well as an interdisciplinary major in biochemistry. The Chemistry major is a strong, foundational degree suitable for students planning to enter the chemical industry or to pursue graduate studies in chemistry.
Accreditation status: Certified by the American Chemical Society (ACS).

description: The B.S. degree with a major in chemistry, which is certified by the American Chemical Society, is designed for students who intend to pursue graduate studies in chemistry, biochemistry or a related field; to pursue a career in the chemical industry; or to pursue a professional career in medicine, dentistry or another health-related field.
Accreditation status: Certified by the American Chemical Society

description: The Children and Youth in Families and Society minor is an interdisciplinary program designed for undergraduate students who are interested in acquiring a knowledge base in social work and social welfare in the U.S. and in developing skills to serve vulnerable children, youth and families. It offers students the opportunity to learn about the social, political, and economic contexts of human needs and services, and the societal responses to them. This minor can complement a number of undergraduate degrees such as public policy, psychology, sociology, women’s studies and education.
Accreditation status: The University of Michigan's Bachelor of Arts with a major in Social Work is accredited by the Council on Social Work Education.

Concentration name: Honors Major in Chinese Language and Culture
description: The Chinese major is designed to give students a solid foundation in the Chinese language, as well as an understanding of Chinese culture and society. The Chinese major includes courses in the Chinese language, literature, linguistics, film, and culture. The requirements are designed to be flexible, so that students can focus on the areas that are of the greatest interest to them, and so that they can easily combine a Chinese major with a major in another field. The Chinese major is administered by the Department of Asian Languages and Cultures.

Concentration name: ['construction engineering and management', 'environmental engineering', 'geotechnical engineering', 'hydraulic and hydrologic engineering', 'materials', 'structural engineering']
description: Civil engineers are responsible for the design, construction, and maintenance of the built environment that is essential to our society. Civil engineers are uniquely equipped to meet the major challenges facing society including the rebuilding and modernization of our infrastructure, creating a sustainable environment, and addressing the impacts of climate change and natural hazards. The work of civil engineers is highly visible and impacts all of our daily lives. This includes our infrastructure (buildings, bridges, roads, and dams), environmental quality (water quality and treatment, air pollution, and waste management), and quality of life (energy systems, transportation systems, and geohazards).
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science in Engineering (BSE) in Civil Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: The major in Classical Archaeology introduces students to the material culture of the ancient Greek and Roman worlds. It is an interdisciplinary major that combines the study of ancient art and archaeology with the study of ancient history and ancient languages. The major is designed to give students a broad introduction to the field of classical archaeology and to provide the basis for a sound liberal arts education; it is also intended to prepare students for graduate work in this and related fields.

The study of Greek and Roman antiquity is an excellent way for students to acquire a liberal arts education. The major in Classical Civilization is an interdisciplinary program that introduces students to the history, literature, art, and archaeology of the ancient Greek and Roman worlds. Majors will learn about the cultures of ancient Greece and Rome, including their languages, literature, history, art, archaeology, philosophy and their lasting impact on the modern world.

The Classical Languages and Literatures major is for students who want to study both Greek and Latin, the core languages of the department. This major provides a great deal of flexibility and provides a comprehensive training in both the ancient languages and the literatures written in them. Students in this major take a combination of courses in Greek, Latin, and classical civilization. Like all of our majors, the CLL major offers a solid preparation for a career in law, medicine, business, and education, and for graduate school in classics and other fields.

Climate and meteorology are two of the most popular and important topics in the physical sciences. Climate science is the study of long-term weather patterns and the forces that cause them to change. The effects of climate change are already being seen in society. Meteorologists are atmospheric scientists who are able to understand and predict the weather. They study the processes and forces that cause weather conditions and use their knowledge to forecast short- and long-term weather patterns. These forecasts are used by government agencies, private companies, and the public. You’ll be prepared for careers in research, government, military, television, and private industry.

Concentration name: Cognition and Computation, Language and Cognition, Philosophy and Cognition
description: Cognitive Science is the interdisciplinary study of the mind. Cognitive scientists study how the mind works and how it produces intelligent behavior. They draw on methods and theories from a wide range of fields, including computer science, linguistics, neuroscience, philosophy, and psychology. The LSA Cognitive Science major is designed for students who want to study the mind from an interdisciplinary perspective. The major provides a broad background in the fundamental issues and methods of cognitive science. Students will learn about topics such as perception, memory, language, reasoning, and consciousness. They will also learn about the different approaches that cognitive scientists use to study the mind, including computational modeling, behavioral experiments, and brain imaging.

Concentration name: ['Media & Entertainment']
description: The Department of Communication and Media at the University of Michigan is an interdisciplinary unit in the College of Literature, Science, and the Arts, linking faculty and students who share a common interest in the study of the media. The Department offers an undergraduate major and minor, and a PhD program. Our curriculum provides students with a liberal arts approach to the study of media institutions, media messages, and the effects of media on society, culture, and individuals. Our students are prepared to be thoughtful and engaged media producers and consumers, and to pursue graduate study or careers in government, business, and the nonprofit sector.

Communication and Media studies the powerful role of media and communication in shaping our world. The field offers a distinctive approach by combining a liberal arts education with hands-on, professionally oriented skills and experiential learning opportunities. Our students graduate with exceptional research, writing, and critical thinking skills, prepared for work in a wide range of industries such as technology, government, entertainment, journalism, public relations, advertising, and marketing.

The undergraduate program at the University of Michigan School of Public Health offers two majors that allow you to explore the many factors that influence human health. Our innovative, action-based curriculum is designed to help you build the skills you need to think critically about health and to develop real-world solutions for the complex challenges we face in today’s world. Both of our majors—the Bachelor of Arts in Community and Global Public Health and the Bachelor of Science in Public Health Sciences—leverage the extensive resources of a world-class university and are taught by leading public health faculty who are passionate about sharing their expertise to help shape the next generation of public health leaders. Whether your passion is in advocacy and policy, community-based health interventions, or epidemiology and data analysis, Michigan Public health will give you the tools to create a healthier world on a local, national, and global scale.

The undergraduate major in comparative literature offers students the opportunity to study literature across the boundaries of language and nation, and to combine literary study with other fields in the humanities, arts, and social sciences. Students in the program work in at least one language other than English and write a senior thesis on a topic of their choice. Recent thesis topics have included: a comparison of European and Arabic traditions of courtly love; the novel of education in France and the US; classical myth in contemporary Caribbean women’s writing; literature and the visual arts in Japanese modernism; and the figure of the cyborg in feminist science fiction. The department offers two honors plans.

Concentration name: Computer Science, Information Systems, Software Engineering
description: The Computer and Information Science (CIS) department at the University of Michigan-Dearborn is at the forefront of the digital revolution. The CIS program curriculum is designed to balance theory and practice, to make students successful in their chosen careers. Courses are kept small, which allows for dedicated attention from our award-winning faculty, and class schedules are designed to meet the needs of today’s students. Through the required internship program, students can find paid, career-related experience as they work with IT professionals at companies such as Ford Motor Co., General Motors, DTE Energy, Quicken Loans, and more. Our graduates have pursued rewarding careers at a broad spectrum of companies, including Amazon, Apple, and Microsoft. Others have pursued graduate studies at universities such as Carnegie-Mellon, Cornell, the University of Michigan, and more.
Accreditation status: The Computer Science concentration is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, www.abet.org.

Concentration name: ['Autonomous Systems and Robotics', 'Bio-systems', 'Communications and Signal Processing', 'Computer Architecture', 'Control Systems', 'Embedded Systems', 'MEMS and Microsystems', 'Optics and Photonics', 'Power and Energy', 'Software', 'Solid-State Devices and Nanotechnology', 'VLSI']
description: As a computer engineer, you can design and build the systems that are changing the world. Computer engineering (CE) at Michigan is a perfect marriage of electrical engineering and computer science, reaching into hardware and software. It’s a field that has enabled the ongoing revolution in information technology, from supercomputers to smartphones, and that will continue to play a critical role as we design the cyber-physical systems of the future. The computer engineering bachelor's degree program is a challenging and rewarding one, offered jointly by the Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) and Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) divisions. It will teach you how to analyze, design, and evaluate computer systems of all shapes and sizes. You can study robotics and artificial intelligence, or data and information systems. You can work with some of the most advanced technology on campus and choose from 10 different technical concentrations. You’ll be prepared for careers in all sectors of the economy: automotive, consumer electronics, medical systems, defense, aerospace, and more.
Accreditation status: The Computer Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description: Computer engineering is the common ground between electrical engineering and computer science. It is concerned with all aspects of computing, from the basic design of a computer to the development of large-scale systems that use computers to control processes and to sense and interact with their physical environment. As a computer engineering student, you will be prepared to create the future of this field, with broad expertise that encompasses computer architecture, embedded systems, networks, and mobile computing.
Accreditation status: The Computer Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description: The Computer Science (CS) program is for students whose primary interest is in the design of computers and computational processes. The CS program provides a foundation in the science of computing and prepares students for a career in the computing field as well as for graduate study. Students will learn about the theoretical and practical aspects of computer science, including algorithms, data structures, programming languages, operating systems, computer architecture, and software engineering. In addition, students will learn how to apply their knowledge to solve real-world problems. The program emphasizes the importance of teamwork, communication, and ethical responsibility in the field of computing. A grade of C or better is required in each course that is a prerequisite for a subsequent Computer Science course.
Accreditation status: The Computer Science program (B.S.E.) is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Computer Science Program Criteria.

Concentration name: AI, databases, graphics, HCI, robotics, security, systems, theory
description: Computer science is the scientific and practical study of computation and its many applications. As a computer science student at U-M, you’ll learn the fundamental concepts of the field as well as how to apply them to real-world problems. You’ll become proficient in several programming languages and familiar with planning, designing, and implementing large software systems. Michigan’s computer science program emphasizes the intellectual substance of the field, and will prepare you for a career in a rapidly changing field or to pursue graduate study in the discipline. You’ll have the opportunity to take courses in topics such as theory of computation, artificial intelligence, databases, computer graphics, computer architecture, operating systems, and software engineering. Offered through the College of Engineering.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science in Engineering degree program in Computer Science is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description: The Creative Writing and Literature major offers students the opportunity to develop their writing in the context of an intensive liberal arts curriculum. Students learn to analyze and respond to a wide range of literary works, while also creating their own. The major supports students’ development in four genres: poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and drama, while allowing them to focus in one of these genres and produce a substantial thesis. Courses are taught by award-winning faculty with extensive publication and performance experience, and who excel in providing a supportive atmosphere for this intimate and intensive work.

Concentration name: Criminology and Criminal Justice
description: This concentration examines the distribution, causes, and consequences of criminal and deviant behavior and the social responses to it. Students study the criminal justice system, legal institutions, juvenile delinquency, deviance, violence, and criminal careers. This area of specialization is well-suited for students who are interested in law, social work, public policy, corrections, and various other professions concerned with the problem of crime in our society.

The Cybersecurity and Information Assurance (CIA) degree is an interdisciplinary program, with the College of Education, Health, and Human Services and the College of Engineering and Computer Science, that focuses on network and information security, secure software engineering, and information assurance. The CIA program provides students with the deep technical skills and knowledge necessary to protect and defend computer systems and networks. In the final two semesters of the program, students participate in a two-semester capstone design experience that brings together teams of students to design and implement a solution to a real-world problem.

The Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) in Dance is a rigorous 128-credit-hour professional degree program. Dance majors take a core curriculum of courses in ballet, modern/contemporary dance, and hip hop dance techniques and creative practices, with additional courses in dance production, music, history, somatics, career development, and pedagogy. Students are given a broad-based liberal arts education through the College of Literature, Science, and the Arts (LSA) and an immersive experience within the dance discipline. The program’s mission is to be on the leading edge of dance in the 21st century by providing a rich environment for students to become exceptional and multifaceted artists, thinkers, and leaders.
Accreditation status: The School of Music, Theatre & Dance is also an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Dance (NASD).

description: Data science is an interdisciplinary field that uses mathematics, statistics, and computer science to gain knowledge and insights from data in all forms. Students will build a strong foundational understanding of the underlying theory behind data science, as well as the practical skills to apply that knowledge to real-world problems. The program integrates statistical, mathematical, and computational thinking, with an emphasis on how data is used in various disciplines and industries, and the ethical issues surrounding data science.

Concentration name: The program requires students to choose an upper-level track from the following: Computer Science Track, Statistics Track, Quantitative Social Science Track, Bioinformatics Track. Students must also complete an area of application, known as a 'concentration', chosen from a different discipline.
description: Data science is the science of learning from data. It involves collecting, managing, processing, analyzing, visualizing, and interpreting data with the goal of extracting knowledge, discovering new insights, making predictions, and supporting decision-making. The major in Data Science at the University of Michigan is jointly offered by the Statistics Department in the College of Literature, Science, and the Arts, and the Electrical Engineering and Computer Science Department in the College of Engineering. All students take a common core of seven courses, plus four more advanced courses called the "upper level track." Data science majors also are required to choose and complete the requirements of a concentration of at least three courses chosen from a different discipline. This allows students to apply data science methods and techniques in an area of their interest.

The U-M School of Dentistry offers two highly regarded programs in dental hygiene: an entry-level Bachelor of Science degree program and a degree completion program for licensed dental hygienists who have an associate’s degree or certificate and wish to complete their bachelor’s degree. There is also an online Master of Science in Dental Hygiene degree program. Our comprehensive and challenging curriculum, our diverse patient care experiences, and our supportive community of faculty, staff, and students prepares our graduates to become leaders in the field.
Accreditation status: The University of Michigan School of Dentistry dental hygiene program is accredited by the Commission on Dental Accreditation (CODA).

description: The Bachelor of Arts in Drama: A Program in Playwriting, Literature, and Dramaturgy is a liberal arts program for students who are passionate about the scholarly study of theatre as a humanistic discipline. The BA in Drama emphasizes critical and creative thinking about theatre and performance, and the development of analytical and communication skills in writing and speaking. The program features a carefully designed sequence of courses in dramatic literature, theatre history, and dramaturgy, with a strong commitment to artistic practice in the form of studio courses in design, directing, playwriting, and performance. In addition to a core curriculum of seven required courses, drama majors enroll in four elective courses that focus on specific areas of interest. This flexible curriculum allows students to explore the ways in which theatre and performance respond to specific cultural, social, and political contexts, both historically and in the present moment. Students learn about the role of theatre in different cultures and communities, including Broadway, regional, and experimental venues. The program encourages students to take advantage of the extraordinary range of academic opportunities and resources that the university as a whole has to offer, including the LSA Course Catalog and study abroad programs. BA in Drama majors are critical and creative thinkers who possess the knowledge and skills necessary for a wide range of academic and professional careers in the arts and beyond.

Concentration name: ['Climate and Surface Processes', 'Earth Science Education', 'Environmental Geology', 'Geology', 'Oceanography', 'Paleontology']
description: The Earth and Environmental Sciences major is the most flexible of the degree programs offered by the department. It is designed for students who want a strong multidisciplinary background in the Earth and environmental sciences, which they may complement with courses from other fields. Students who complete the major receive a Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree from the College of Literature, Science, and the Arts.

The major in Ecology, Evolution, and Biodiversity (EEB) is designed for students with an interest in the biological disciplines that focus on the origins, diversity, and history of life, and the dynamic relationships of living organisms with their environments. Majors receive a Bachelor of Science degree. The major is one of the most flexible in the biological sciences, with only a few specific required courses. Students choose from a wide variety of courses spanning the breadth of ecology and evolutionary biology, including such topics as animal behavior, conservation biology, population genetics, systematics, tropical biology, and quantitative ecology. Students are exposed to both field and laboratory approaches to research and are strongly encouraged to become directly involved in research at U-M or at one of the university's biological stations. After graduation, EEB majors are well prepared for careers or graduate studies in a number of areas, including ecology, evolutionary biology, conservation biology and environmental science, medicine, dentistry, and other health sciences, natural resources management, education, museum studies, and many others.

Concentration name: Mathematical Economics and Econometrics
description: Economics is a social science that analyzes how choices are made by individuals, firms, and governments, and how these decisions determine the allocation of scarce resources and the distribution of well-being in a society. Economics offers a powerful and broad framework for understanding the world in which we live and work, providing insights into a wide range of important social and political issues, including unemployment, inflation, economic growth, international trade and finance, poverty, income inequality, environmental protection, health care, and education. Students of economics develop strong analytical and quantitative reasoning skills and an ability to communicate complex ideas effectively, skills that are highly valued in the marketplace and that provide an excellent foundation for a wide range of career paths and graduate degree programs.

Economics is a social science that deals with the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services. A primary goal of the discipline is to determine how to use scarce resources to satisfy people's wants and needs in the best way possible. At the undergraduate level, an economics major is designed to provide students with a firm grounding in the principles of economic analysis. The core of the curriculum involves study in the areas of microeconomics (the study of individual decision-making and market outcomes), macroeconomics (the study of the behavior of the entire economy), and econometrics (the application of statistical methods to economic data).

The BS in Economics and Computation, or 'Econ-Comp,' is an innovative, interdisciplinary major jointly offered by the Departments of Economics and Computer Science. The major aims to equip students with the foundational skills to analyze and design the digital marketplaces and platforms that are increasingly central to modern economic and social life (e.g., social media, online dating apps, ride-sharing, online ad auctions, cryptocurrencies). A key feature of the major is a two-semester capstone sequence, Econ 407/408, in which students design and build a digital platform or marketplace of their own. Other highlights of the curriculum include an innovative new course, Econ/CS 376: Normative and Behavioral Approaches to Market Design, which integrates foundational topics from economics and computer science, including game theory, social choice, and machine learning.

Concentration name: Elementary Teacher Education, Learning, Equity, and Problem Solving in the Public Interest (LEAPS), Secondary Teacher Education
description: The Bachelor of Arts (A.B.) in Education degree program offers three distinct majors, two in elementary education and one in secondary education. Elementary Teacher Education focuses on teaching children in grades K-8. Learning, Equity, and Problem Solving in the Public Interest (LEAPS) offers two pathways for those who are interested in creating learning environments both in and beyond schools. Students in the first pathway can become certified elementary teachers, and students in the second pathway will work in education-related, non-school contexts. Secondary Teacher Education is for those who wish to teach a specific subject in grades 6-12. The Marsal School also has one minor program in education for social change.
Accreditation status: The Marsal Family School of Education at the University of Michigan is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP). The Marsal School is also a Teacher Preparation Institution approved by the Michigan Department of Education (MDE).

description: Electrical engineering is a broad field, encompassing a wide variety of devices, systems, and technologies that impact our everyday lives. Electrical engineers design and build devices and systems for a variety of applications, such as computing, communications, sensing, and energy. Students can tailor their program to their interests by selecting a major design experience course and technical electives from areas like: analog/RF circuits, communications, computer vision, control systems, electromagnetics, embedded systems, integrated circuit design, machine learning, MEMS and microsystems, optics and photonics, power and energy, robotics, signal and image processing, and solid-state devices. Note: Admission to the College of Engineering is a two-step process. Students must first be admitted to the college as a first-year or external transfer student. After they have completed the first-year curriculum, students will be able to declare their engineering major. Because there are enrollment limits for each major, the major may not be available at the time of enrollment.
Accreditation status: The Electrical Engineering undergraduate program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

Concentration name: Analog and Mixed Signal Circuits, Communications, Computer Architecture and Design, Control Systems, Electromagnetics and Optics, Embedded Systems, MEMS and Microsystems, Power and Energy, Robotics, Signal and Image Processing and Machine Learning, Solid State and Nanotechnology
description: Electrical engineers focus on the generation, transmission, and use of information and energy. They develop circuits, systems, and software to provide new products and services in areas such as communications, control, electronics, sensing, and power and energy.
Accreditation status: The Electrical Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description: The elementary Teacher Education (TE) program at the University of Michigan’s Marsal Family School of Education prepares you to become a certified elementary school teacher. The elementary TE program offers three pathways to earn a bachelor’s degree with elementary teacher certification. The first two pathways are intended for first-year applicants to U-M, and the third pathway is for transfer students (both internal and external). No matter which pathway a student follows, they complete the same rigorous teacher education coursework, including extensive, high-quality field experiences in elementary schools throughout southeastern Michigan. You will be prepared to teach grades K–8 in all subjects in a self-contained classroom. You can also add on a middle school subject area endorsement to your teaching certificate.
Accreditation status: The Marsal Family School of Education at the University of Michigan is accredited by the Association for Advancing Quality in Educator Preparation (AAQEP).

Concentration name: ['Language Arts', 'Mathematics', 'Integrated Science', 'Social Studies']
description: The Elementary Teacher Education (ELMAC) program leads to a bachelor's degree with elementary teacher certification (K-8). The program is designed for students who want to become classroom teachers in diverse contexts. You will learn how to teach all elementary subjects and select an academic area to earn an endorsement in that subject on your teaching certificate. Our teacher education programs prepare you to understand and respect the integrity of children from a diversity of backgrounds and to create challenging and supportive learning environments for them. You will work with expert faculty in a diverse cohort of peer learners. You will engage in real-world teaching experiences in K-8 school settings to learn to connect theory with practice. We are committed to developing educators who will make a positive difference in the lives of children and youth and in the communities they serve.
Accreditation status: The Marsal Family School of Education at the University of Michigan is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP).

description: Engineering Physics is for students who have a passion for both physics and engineering. The program combines a core of physics and mathematics courses with a concentration of engineering courses. The curriculum provides a strong background in the fundamentals of science and mathematics and a firm understanding of engineering methods. You can choose to concentrate in a specific area of engineering, or develop a unique course of study with the help of a faculty advisor. The program prepares students to solve complex problems at the intersection of different disciplines in industry or in graduate school.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

Concentration name: ['Creative Writing', 'Great Books', 'Honors', 'Textual and Digital Studies']
description: As an English major at the University of Michigan, you will receive an education both broad and deep in the literature and cultures of the English-speaking world. In our courses, you will learn to read and think critically not only about literature but about the world around you. You will also develop skill in both analytical and creative writing. Our department is committed to the values of diversity and inclusion, which are reflected throughout our curriculum. English is among the most versatile of liberal arts majors. Our students are prepared to follow a very wide variety of career paths, and to meet the demand for broadly educated people who can write and think well. English majors have gone on to careers in law, business, medicine, journalism, publishing, advertising, teaching, and technology.

Concentration name: ['Creative Writing', 'Great Books', 'Honors Program', 'Language and Literature', 'Writing']
description: The English major at the University of Michigan is for students who love to read and write, and who want to do so in a way that is informed by literary history, critical methodologies, and a deep understanding of the English language. All of our courses are designed to develop students’ abilities to read critically, think analytically, and write with power and precision. The English Major leads to a Bachelor of Arts (A.B.) degree and provides an excellent foundation for any career. Our majors go on to law school and medical school, business and education, publishing and marketing, and the creative and performing arts. Students may focus their studies in a number of areas, or they can pursue a more general interest in literature and culture.

The Minor in Entrepreneurship is a joint initiative between the College of Engineering and the Stephen M. Ross School of Business. It is open to undergraduate students from any school or college. A passion for creating and launching new ventures—commercial, social, or corporate—is the unifying theme that brings students together in the program. Students learn how to turn ideas into value-creating enterprises. The minor integrates experiential learning, providing students with the knowledge and experience to be successful entrepreneurs.

Concentration name: Conservation & Ecology, Earth, Climate & Energy, Environmental Humanities & Arts, Environmental Justice & Policy, Environmental Science & Society, Food & the Environment, Sustainability & Business, Water & the Great Lakes
description: The Environment major, offered through the Program in the Environment (PitE), allows students to simultaneously pursue a liberal arts education and a pre-professional program in the environmental field. The curriculum provides a broad interdisciplinary education in the liberal arts and sciences, as well as an opportunity to develop expertise in an area of environmental study in one of five specializations. Students in the major may earn a B.A. degree in Environment through the College of Literature, Science, and the Arts (LSA) or a B.S. degree in Environment through the School for Environment and Sustainability (SEAS). In addition to coursework, students have an opportunity to participate in a variety of off-campus and research opportunities as well as a vibrant student community.

Concentration name: ['Water Quality and Process Engineering', 'Sustainable Engineering']
description: Environmental engineers are on the front lines, protecting our environment from the effects of human activities and designing sustainable engineering solutions for a better tomorrow. Environmental engineers are involved in a variety of important tasks, such as designing systems to provide safe drinking water, collecting and treating wastewater to protect our waterways, managing solid and hazardous wastes, controlling air pollution, cleaning up contaminated sites, and helping industries to minimize their pollution. They are also involved in setting environmental policy and regulations, and ensuring compliance. Students gain a strong foundation in science and engineering fundamentals, as well as an in-depth understanding of the complex interactions between humans and our environment. Core coursework emphasizes chemistry, biology, geology, and engineering principles related to water quality, air quality, and sustainable use of natural resources. The program also provides flexibility to allow students to pursue individual interests. The department offers two concentrations to provide students with more advanced technical skills in certain environmental sub-disciplines. The department offers many domestic and international environmental experiential learning opportunities.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science in Engineering (BSE) programs in Civil Engineering and in Environmental Engineering are accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

Concentration name: Biology, Chemistry, Geology, Physics
description: The Environmental Science major, offered by the Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences (EARTH) and the Program in the Environment (PitE), provides students with a strong background in natural sciences and a robust understanding of the scientific principles and methodologies required to understand and solve complex environmental problems. The major is interdisciplinary and offers coursework from several departments across campus. The curriculum includes a rigorous sequence of introductory courses in the natural sciences, mathematics, and statistics, followed by two broad core courses in environmental science, and then specialization in a specific area of environmental science in the upper-level concentration. Coursework emphasizes an integrative approach to problem solving, hands-on experience in the field and laboratory, and the application of modern research tools to environmental issues.

Concentration name: Sub-major in Screenwriting
description: The Department of Film, Television, and Media (FTVM) provides an integrated program of study in the history, theory, and practice of these three media forms. FTVM offers a range of introductory and advanced courses covering the entire spectrum of film, television, and media, from the silent era to the digital age. The department's production courses provide hands-on training in 16mm filmmaking, digital video, and screenwriting. Internships are available in Ann Arbor, Detroit, New York, Los Angeles, and London. FTVM majors go on to successful careers in the media industries, as well as in such related fields as advertising, public relations, arts administration, and education. Many pursue graduate degrees in law, business, and media studies. The department sponsors a variety of special events, including the 16mm Film Festival and the biennial P. Adams Sitney lecture, and regularly brings distinguished filmmakers, television producers, screenwriters, and media scholars to campus.

Provides a conceptual framework for understanding and analyzing major financial decisions. Students develop analytical and decision-making skills in the context of financial markets and institutions, investments, and corporate finance.

Concentration name: Honors Major
description: The undergraduate curriculum in French and Francophone Studies is designed to give students a thorough grounding in the language and a broad introduction to French and Francophone literatures and cultures. By developing an ability to speak and write French and to read with a critical eye, students will gain a deeper understanding of French and Francophone cultures. They will also acquire the tools to see their own culture from a new perspective. Students often complement their studies in French with coursework in Art History, Comparative Literature, Film, History, Music, Philosophy, or Political Science. Students may choose to major, major with honors, or minor in French and Francophone Studies.

Concentration name: Honors Major
description: The French major at the University of Michigan focuses on the language, literature, and culture of France and the Francophone world. Students develop a high level of proficiency in French and gain an in-depth understanding of the rich and diverse cultures of French-speaking countries. The French major prepares students for graduate school in French or related fields, for professional school in fields like law, business, or medicine, for careers in education, and for the many positions in government and the private sector where knowledge of a second language and culture is an essential or desirable qualification.

Ross students are immersed in an action-based curriculum in which they take on real-world business challenges from day one. In every class and every project, they are encouraged to experiment, take risks, and learn from their mistakes. The BBA curriculum features a core program that provides a strong foundation in all areas of business: accounting, finance, strategy, marketing, management, operations, and business law and ethics. After establishing this strong foundation, students have the option to pursue one or more Areas of Emphasis, although an Area of Emphasis is not required for graduation. All BBAs also complete an international business experience and a capstone project that addresses a current issue facing a real-world company or organization.
Accreditation status: Accredited by AACSB International - The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business

Concentration name: Honors Major in German, Business German, German for Engineering
description: German at Michigan does not just mean Germany. Our program is broadly conceived to give students access to the rich cultural traditions of the German-speaking world as a whole, including Austria and Switzerland. While language acquisition is the foundation for all further work, the curriculum offers a broad spectrum of courses in English and German on literature, culture, history, film, and intellectual history. Our small classes provide an excellent environment for learning in a supportive and challenging community of students and faculty. U-M also offers a minor in German Studies and Dutch Studies.

The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Global Environment and Health provides students with a strong foundation in environmental health sciences, focusing on the environmental factors that impact human health and the spread of disease. Students will learn about the interconnectedness of environmental and human health through multiple lenses including toxicology, infectious disease, risk assessment, environmental justice and policy. This major addresses the interaction between the environment and humans at a global scale, including topics such as climate change, water quality, and food safety, while preparing students to understand how these global issues impact our local communities. Students have the opportunity to engage in a research or internship experience to gain hands-on skills in environmental health. Graduates from this major are equipped with the skills and knowledge to pursue careers in a variety of industries that focus on improving human health.

The study of Greek language and literature involves a dynamic and complex set of disciplines that have as their common focus the life and culture of ancient Greece. This rigorous liberal arts program trains students to evaluate literary and historical evidence, to form independent judgments, and to articulate and defend their ideas. By the end of the program, students will have an advanced knowledge of Greek language and literature and a deep understanding of ancient Greek culture. Majors are encouraged to enrich their programs with courses in related fields, such as philosophy, history, history of art, and political science.

The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Health and Fitness is a degree designed for students whose primary interest is in the scientific basis of health and fitness. This program prepares students for careers related to exercise and health maintenance for the general population. Students are prepared to assess fitness, design and implement exercise programs, and understand basic business management and marketing principles as they apply to the health and fitness industries.

Concentration name: Public Health, Community Health Education and Health Care Administration
description: The Health and Human Services (HHS) major at UM-Dearborn provides students with an interdisciplinary curriculum that draws upon a unique combination of courses in health sciences, social sciences, and professional studies. The curriculum is delivered within a framework of community engagement and service-learning. Students gain a diverse knowledge of the human services field with a special emphasis on health promotion and health equity in community-based and public health care settings. Concentrations in Public Health, Community Health Education and Health Care Administration offer students career flexibility in settings ranging from hospitals and community clinics to local health departments, non-profits and private health care facilities.

Concentration name: Spanish, Spanish-American Studies
description: Hispanic Studies is the study of the languages, literatures, and cultures of the Spanish-speaking peoples of Europe, North, Central and South America, the Caribbean, and North Africa. Hispanic Studies encompasses a vast and diverse region of the world with an extremely rich literary and cultural heritage. The Hispanic Studies major provides students with a solid foundation in the languages, literatures, and cultures of the Spanish-speaking world while affording them the flexibility to tailor their program of study to their individual interests and career plans. Hispanic Studies at Michigan is housed in the Department of Romance Languages and Literatures, which also offers a major and minor in Romance Languages and Literatures and a minor in Translation Studies. Students in the Hispanic Studies major may elect a concentration in Spanish or Spanish-American Studies at the undergraduate level, or they may combine courses in both areas. The Hispanic Studies major has been revised to reflect current scholarship in the field, so that the curriculum now integrates the study of literature and culture. In addition, students have the opportunity to participate in a variety of faculty-led study abroad programs, or to design their own course of study abroad. The department also encourages students to undertake an honors thesis in their senior year.

Concentration name: History Honors Major
description: The study of history is the study of the human past, in all its variety and complexity. We seek to understand how people have lived, acted, and thought in different times and places. We ask how societies have been structured, how they have changed over time, and how they have related to one another. We explore the cultures people have created, the ideas they have held, and the struggles they have engaged in. By studying history, we gain a deeper understanding of ourselves and our world. A major in history will equip you with the skills to think critically, to write persuasively, and to conduct independent research. These skills are essential for success in any field, and they will prepare you for a wide range of careers.

The History major is designed to provide students with a broad introduction to the study of the human past, while also affording them the opportunity to pursue in-depth study of the particular periods and places that most interest them. The requirements for the major encourage a great deal of intellectual exploration but are also meant to ensure that our students graduate with a coherent plan of study that has been developed in consultation with a faculty advisor. The result is an excellent liberal arts education that prepares students for a variety of careers in fields such as law, business, education, journalism, public service, and many others. Those planning to go on to graduate study in history will also find that the major provides the foundation they need to succeed.

The History of Art underlies a liberal arts education, giving you critical tools for analyzing and contextualizing the world around you. At U-M, we study a broad range of art, architecture, and visual and material culture from around the globe, spanning from the ancient to the contemporary. Classes are small, with most capped at 25 students, and our majors and minors have opportunities for first-hand study of objects in U-M's renowned museums and special collections. Our flexible undergraduate program allows students to combine their study of art history with pre-professional tracks or double majors in a wide range of fields. History of Art majors are successful in an array of careers, including law, medicine, art conservation, museum and gallery work, publishing, marketing, and design.

Human-centered engineering design is a problem-solving process that prioritizes the needs of people. It is based on the idea that the most effective and successful products and services are created when designers have a deep understanding of the people they are designing for. Students in this program will learn how to conduct user research, identify user needs, and develop creative solutions to meet those needs. They will also learn how to work in teams to design and build prototypes of their solutions. The program culminates in a capstone project in which students work on a real-world design challenge.

Concentration name: Human Resource Management
description: The Michigan Ross Bachelor of Business Administration is a top-ranked, immersive undergraduate business program that provides a comprehensive business education, action-based learning, and a broad-based liberal arts foundation. You will be challenged to start, advise, and lead real-world businesses and projects through a curriculum designed for you to learn business by doing business. You’ll gain a deep understanding of business fundamentals, including accounting, finance, marketing, and strategy, along with the flexibility to pursue a variety of academic interests and passions.
Accreditation status: Michigan Ross is accredited by the AACSB.

description: Industrial and Operations Engineering (IOE) is the data-driven approach to making systems and processes better, faster, safer and more efficient. IOE combines skills from engineering, math, statistics, and social sciences to solve real-world problems. U-M IOE’s mission is to provide an exceptional and innovative educational experience, to create and communicate new knowledge, and to provide extraordinary leadership and service in the industrial and operations engineering profession.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET

description: As an industrial and operations engineer, you will learn to utilize techniques from engineering, mathematics, and psychology to make systems and processes more efficient.
