Industrial and operations engineers work in every sector of the economy — from developing more efficient patient flow in hospitals to streamlining production in factories. This major stresses a multi-disciplinary approach to solving problems and creating efficient systems.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET.

description: The Information Systems (IS) area at Ross is a research-oriented group focused on understanding the economic, organizational, and social implications of information technology. The curriculum focuses on giving students a broad perspective on the business opportunities and challenges represented by the rapid and pervasive developments in information technology. Our courses provide an overview of the role of information systems in organizations; an introduction to information technology, data management, and business analytics; and in-depth coverage of topics including information systems strategy, design, and implementation.

The Instructional Design and Learning Technologies (IDLT) degree focuses on designing, developing, implementing, and evaluating instruction for various contexts, including K-12, higher education, corporate, nonprofit, and government settings. The program is designed to develop students' knowledge and skills in learning theory, instructional design models, and technologies for learning. Students will engage in coursework and experiences that will develop their skills in areas such as learning analysis, instructional design and development for a variety of formats (e.g., in-person, blended, online), program evaluation, and project management. Students will complete a design-based internship as a capstone experience and will develop a professional portfolio. With the increasing reliance on online training and development, the IDLT degree is ideal for students who want to develop practical, in-demand skills and an understanding of how to apply the science of learning to a variety of contexts.
Program name: Instructional Design and Learning Technologies, AB

description: The Integrative Studies (IS) program provides an excellent opportunity for students to individualize their course of study and create a degree program that meets their personal interests and career goals. The IS program is designed for students who have a specific interest that is not adequately covered by a single major or who have a broad interest that spans several academic departments. In the IS program, students can create an individualized course of study that combines courses from two or three academic areas.

Concentration name: Biochemistry, Biophysical Chemistry, Chemical Physics, Environmental Chemistry, Materials Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Chemistry
description: The Interdisciplinary Chemical Sciences (ICS) major is designed to provide a strong foundation in chemistry, while allowing students sufficient flexibility to explore interdisciplinary interests. The core requirements for the ICS major consist of foundational coursework in chemistry, mathematics, and physics, as well as core coursework in the four primary areas of chemistry: analytical, inorganic, organic, and physical chemistry. The flexible portion of the ICS curriculum consists of a minimum of 18 credits of advanced coursework in chemistry and related areas of science and/or engineering, with at least 9 of these credits taken in the Chemistry Department. The advanced electives are chosen by the student with the assistance of a chemistry faculty advisor to form a coherent program that is consistent with the student's interests and career goals. Students may pursue a general course of study or may design a more focused program with a specific emphasis in a number of areas, including Biochemistry, Biophysical Chemistry, Chemical Physics, Environmental Chemistry, Materials Chemistry, or Pharmaceutical Chemistry. Students in the Honors Program may elect an Honors ICS major.

The Interdisciplinary Physics major is designed for students who want to combine a strong background in physics with a significant number of courses in a related field. The Interdisciplinary Physics major is appropriate for students who are interested in areas such as biophysics, chemical physics, geophysics, mathematical physics, medical physics, or astrophysics.

Concentration name: ['Comparative Culture and Identity (CCI)', 'Global Environment and Health (GEH)', 'International Security, Norms and Cooperation (SNC)', 'Political Economy and Development (PED)', 'Global Coursework (GC) Sub-plan']
description: The major in International Studies is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a sophisticated understanding of our increasingly interconnected world. The International Studies major provides a solid foundation for a variety of careers in government, the private sector, and non-profit organizations, as well as for admission to graduate and professional schools. Students focus on one of six sub-plans within the major to gain depth in their studies. All majors develop advanced language proficiency and build cross-cultural understanding through an international experience.

Concentration name: International Security, Norms & Cooperation; Political Economy & Development; Comparative Culture & Identity; Global Environment & Health; Latin American & Caribbean Studies; European Studies; Middle Eastern & North African Studies; South Asian Studies; or Southeast Asian Studies
description: The Program in International and Comparative Studies (PICS) offers an interdisciplinary liberal arts major leading to a Bachelor of Arts degree. The International Studies major provides students with a multifaceted understanding of the world, including the historical, political, economic, and cultural connections and conflicts that have shaped our world. The International Studies major is comprised of a primary major and one of nine sub-plans: International Security, Norms & Cooperation; Political Economy & Development; Comparative Culture & Identity; Global Environment & Health; Latin American & Caribbean Studies; European Studies; Middle Eastern & North African Studies; South Asian Studies; or Southeast Asian Studies. Students who major in International Studies may not double major in any of the other majors offered in PICS, including the LSA majors in Latin American and Caribbean Studies, Middle Eastern and North African Studies and Modern Middle Eastern and North African Studies.

The Italian major introduces students to Italy’s vital role within a globalized world. You’ll become proficient in the Italian language, and through courses on film, literature, art, history, and politics, you’ll develop a nuanced understanding of Italian society. Our close-knit community of faculty and students will support you as you immerse yourself in an exciting foreign culture, and in doing so, reflect more deeply upon your own. An Italian major can be combined with any other field of study and is particularly useful for students interested in international studies, art history, classical studies, music, business, and political science.

Concentration name: ['Performance', 'Improvisation', 'Jazz Composition', 'Jazz and Contemporary Improvisation with Teacher Certification']
description: The bachelor of fine arts in jazz & contemporary improvisation is a highly specialized and rigorous four-year course of study for students who demonstrate exceptional promise as jazz artists. A strong undergraduate liberal arts component is interwoven with intensive training in jazz and contemporary improvisation performance, arranging, composition, and history, along with foundational instruction in music theory, musicology, and piano.

The Journalism and Media Production major at UM-Dearborn combines a liberal arts education with professional training to prepare students for careers in media industries and for graduate school. Students have many opportunities for hands-on experience through the student-run newspaper, The Michigan Journal, the student-run radio station, WUMD, and through internships with local media companies. The major provides a background for careers in online, print, and broadcast journalism, in public relations, and in corporate, non-profit, and government communications.

The major in Judaic Studies is an interdisciplinary liberal arts major intended to give students a broad-based knowledge of Judaic civilization and the Jewish people from antiquity to the present. The curriculum provides an appreciation of the multi-faceted nature of Jewish culture and its impact on world civilization. The program prepares students for graduate work in Judaic studies and related fields as well as careers in Jewish communal service, Jewish education, and the rabbinate. It also provides a strong liberal arts background for any career or profession a student might choose to pursue.

Students who minor in Korean Studies will develop a broad-based knowledge of Korean culture and society. In order to declare a minor in Korean Studies, students must take a combination of language and culture courses totaling at least 15 credits. At least three of the courses must be taken at the 300 level or above. No more than two language courses may be used to meet the minor requirements. All courses must be passed with a grade of C or better. Students must also maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0. Courses used to satisfy minor requirements may not be taken Pass/Fail.

Landscape architects analyze natural systems and create environmentally sensitive places for people that are both functional and beautiful. The undergraduate program in landscape architecture is a professional degree program that integrates knowledge of art, science, and technology. Students in landscape architecture take a variety of courses within the School for Environment and Sustainability (SEAS) and in other schools and colleges on campus. Coursework focuses on building a foundation of ecological knowledge and developing creative design and technical skills. In design studios, students address real-world challenges through hands-on, project-based learning. In the summer between their junior and senior years, students are required to complete an internship to gain professional experience. Graduates of the BLA program are prepared to enter professional offices, and after a few years of experience, may be eligible for licensure. Graduates pursue work in the private, public, and non-profit sectors in roles such as landscape architects, urban designers, environmental planners, and ecological designers.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Landscape Architecture (BLA) degree is accredited by the Landscape Architectural Accreditation Board (LAAB).

description: The Program in Latin American and Caribbean Studies (LACS) is an interdisciplinary undergraduate program devoted to the study of the histories, cultures, and societies of Latin America and the Caribbean. LACS offers students the flexibility to explore the region from the perspective of many different disciplines and departments at the university, including Afroamerican and African studies, anthropology, comparative literature, history, history of art, political science, romance languages and literatures, and sociology. Our core faculty has expertise in Brazil, the Caribbean, and Spanish America. The interdisciplinary framework of the LACS program allows students to develop an individualized course of study that reflects their specific interests in the region. LACS students learn to think critically and comparatively about the region's shared history of colonialism and its aftermath, and to appreciate the variety and complexity of its societies.

The major in Latin Language and Literature provides students with a rigorous training in the fundamentals of the Latin language and a sophisticated training in how to read, understand, and interpret Latin literary texts in their historical and cultural contexts. At the same time, the major allows students the flexibility to explore a variety of different approaches to the ancient world and to combine their interest in Latin with their interests in other fields.

The Latina/o Studies Program at the University of Michigan provides students with an interdisciplinary approach to the study of Latina/o experiences in the United States. Courses examine the histories, cultures, and intellectual traditions of a population that has its roots in Latin America and the Caribbean, and that has been transformed by its incorporation into American society. The program provides an opportunity for students to complement a traditional disciplinary major or to pursue a Latina/o Studies major by selecting courses from a variety of fields, including American culture, anthropology, communications, comparative literature, English, film and video, history, history of art, music, political science, Romance languages and literatures, social work, sociology, and women's studies.

Concentration name: Language and Computers, Language and Mind, Language and Society, Language and Meaning, Structure of Language
description: The major in Linguistics is designed to introduce students to the methods and subject matter of the scientific study of the human language capacity. Linguistics is a broadly interdisciplinary field that connects to the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences. A major in Linguistics can be a valuable part of a liberal arts education, opening up connections to a wide range of other fields of study. It also provides a strong background for graduate study in linguistics and other related fields (e.g., anthropology, communication, law, philosophy, psychology, language teaching, speech-language pathology, computer science, and artificial intelligence). Finally, it can be valuable preparation for a wide variety of careers.

Concentration name: Management
description: The Management emphasis at Ross builds on a strong foundation in organizational theory and behavior to provide students with the ability to build and lead organizations that succeed. Management is the process of getting things done effectively and efficiently, with and through other people. The best managers excel at a wide variety of skills that can be grouped under four main functions: planning, organizing, leading, and controlling. For this emphasis, students select from a variety of courses within strategy and management and organizations that cover these topics and more.
Accreditation status: The Stephen M. Ross School of Business at the University of Michigan is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB). The first accreditation was in 1919.

description: Students can earn a Bachelor of Science in Engineering (BSE) in Manufacturing Engineering. Manufacturing is the process of converting raw materials into a finished product. This conversion process includes product design, process design, operations, and logistics. Manufacturing engineering education must be a balance between engineering science and industrial practice. This program has an interdisciplinary flavor with a strong core of manufacturing courses.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science in Engineering in Manufacturing Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description: Marketing is more than just selling and advertising; it is a complex and comprehensive function in an organization. Marketing managers are responsible for a wide range of activities that include marketing research, product development, pricing, and management of the channels of distribution, as well as the design of effective advertising, personal selling, and other promotional activities. A successful career in marketing requires both creativity and strong analytical skills. The marketing curriculum is designed to introduce students to the key marketing concepts and to build the analytical and decision-making skills required for a professional career in marketing management or for further graduate study in the field. Students can obtain a bachelor of business administration (BBA) through the Stephen M. Ross School of Business.

Concentration name: Functional and structural materials, Polymers and computational materials science
description: From the cars we drive to the electronic devices in our pockets to the biomedical implants in our bodies, materials are all around us. Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) is an interdisciplinary field that studies the connections between the underlying structure of a material, its properties, how it is made, and what it can do. As a materials scientist and engineer, you can design and create novel materials with new and exciting properties for just about any application you can imagine. Want to design a new lightweight composite for a more fuel-efficient airplane? Or a better biocompatible material for an artificial hip? Or how about a new semiconductor material for a faster computer chip? A degree in MSE will equip you with the fundamental knowledge and skills you need to solve these problems and more. At Michigan, our undergraduate students gain a strong foundation in the fundamentals of materials science and engineering. They go on to work in a diverse range of industries, including aerospace, automotive, electronics, energy, and biomedical devices. Many also go on to graduate school to pursue advanced degrees in MSE or related fields.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET

description: The Mathematical Sciences major is an interdisciplinary major intended for students interested in the applications of mathematics to other fields. Mathematical Sciences is the study of the language of the sciences, including its development, its abstract structures, and its applications. It encompasses traditional mathematics and a number of related fields. It uses the tools of mathematics, computing, and other fields to solve problems from the physical and biological sciences, engineering, and the social and behavioral sciences. Students who choose the Mathematical Sciences major will develop their ability to solve problems, reason abstractly, and communicate their ideas to others. The curriculum is flexible and can be tailored to an individual student's interests. The program is offered jointly by the Departments of Mathematics, Statistics, and Electrical Engineering and Computer Science.

From making sense of big data to creating the algorithms that power our technology, mathematics provides the language we use to understand — and shape — the world. As a mathematics student at Michigan, you will develop rigorous critical thinking and problem-solving skills to meet the challenges of the 21st century. Students are able to create their own path of study by choosing from pure and applied math or a combination of both. The department offers several degree programs for students who want to study mathematics, including Actuarial Mathematics, Financial Mathematics, and Mathematical Sciences. The mathematics curriculum pairs well with a number of different subjects for students who are interested in interdisciplinary study. Popular double majors include: computer science, statistics, economics, and physics.

The Mathematics major is an introduction to the main branches of modern mathematics: algebra, analysis, and geometry/topology. The curriculum is designed to provide students with a broad and deep understanding of the subject, and to develop the thinking skills that are essential for a wide variety of careers. The department offers a wide variety of courses that enable students to explore different areas of mathematics and to tailor their studies to their interests and goals. Students have considerable freedom in designing their major program, and may choose from several tracks, including a standard track, an honors track, a teaching certificate track, and a financial/actuarial track. The financial/actuarial track is designed to prepare students for careers in finance and actuarial science. The teaching certificate track is designed to prepare students for careers in secondary school teaching.

Concentration name: Energy Concentration, Manufacturing Concentration, Pre-med Concentration
description: Mechanical Engineering (ME) is one of the broadest engineering disciplines. ME is the original 'general' engineering degree; its graduates can be found across all industrial sectors and in leadership roles in academia, industry and government. U-M ME students work to solve global challenges involving energy, manufacturing, transportation, health and the environment. Some of our major research areas include: automotive, biomechanics, controls, design, dynamics, energy, fluids, manufacturing, mechanics, mechatronics, and transportation. The U-M ME undergraduate program is consistently ranked among the top programs in the nation.
Accreditation status: The undergraduate program in Mechanical Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

Concentration name: Automotive, Biomechanics, Controls & Robotics, Energy & Power, Manufacturing, Thermal & Fluid Sciences
description: Mechanical engineering is one of the broadest engineering disciplines and is central to the design and manufacturing of nearly every product. Mechanical engineers are employed in almost every industry, from aerospace to automotive, and from biotechnology to computer and electronics. They are involved in research and development, design, manufacturing, and technical sales of a wide variety of products. Some specific examples include: designing medical devices, such as artificial hearts and prosthetic limbs; developing new sustainable energy systems, from wind turbines to solar power; and designing the next generation of automobiles and spacecraft. The undergraduate curriculum provides students with a strong background in the fundamental sciences and in engineering, as well as a broad introduction to all major areas of mechanical engineering. This allows students to tailor their curriculum to their own interests in the junior and senior years, with technical elective courses in areas such as: automotive, biomechanics, controls, design, energy, fluids, heat transfer, manufacturing, and robotics.
Accreditation status: The University of Michigan Mechanical Engineering undergraduate program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

Concentration name: Robotics, Mechatronics, Control Systems
description: Mechatronics and Robotics Engineering (MRE) is a multidisciplinary program that combines the principles of mechanical, electrical, computer, and software engineering. It focuses on the design and development of smart products with a built-in intelligence. Such products are found in a wide variety of industries including manufacturing, automotive, aerospace, defense, consumer products, and healthcare. Robotics is an important application area of mechatronics that deals with the design and operation of robots. The field of robotics is predicted to become one of the most dynamic areas of science and technology in the 21st century. The MRE curriculum at UM-Dearborn provides students with a solid foundation in the underlying principles of mechatronics and robotics, and a broad background to succeed in a wide range of industries.
Accreditation status: The Mechatronics and Robotics Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

Concentration name: Medieval studies, Early Modern studies
description: The Program in Medieval and Early Modern Studies (MEMS) at the University of Michigan is an interdisciplinary program designed for students who wish to study the period from late antiquity to the early 18th century. MEMS students design their own major or minor, in consultation with the program advisor, from courses in more than 20 departments across the university. Majors choose to concentrate in either Medieval or Early Modern studies and are free to study any geographical region during those periods. Minors take one required course (MEMS 250), an introductory course to the period, and choose electives from a wide range of topics.

Concentration name: Microbial Biotechnology, Microbes and Health, Environmental and Evolutionary Microbiology
description: The Microbiology major is for students interested in the study of microorganisms, such as bacteria and viruses. The major provides a firm foundation in the fundamentals of microbial life, including physiology, genetics, and pathogenesis. It also provides laboratory training in both classical and contemporary microbiological methods. Students can choose to pursue a general course of study in microbiology or they can elect to specialize in one of three areas: microbial biotechnology, microbes and health, or environmental and evolutionary microbiology. The major prepares students for graduate study in microbiology or related fields (e.g., molecular biology, immunology, public health) and for professional school (e.g., medical, dental, pharmacy). It is also excellent preparation for careers in the biotechnology, pharmaceutical, or food industries.

Microbiology is the study of microscopic organisms, including bacteria, viruses, fungi, and protozoa. It involves the study of their structure, function, genetics, and ecology, as well as their roles in human health, disease, and the environment. Students in this major gain a strong foundation in the biological and chemical sciences, and they have the opportunity to participate in research with faculty members. Graduates are prepared for a variety of careers in research, healthcare, biotechnology, and other fields, as well as for graduate and professional school.

The major in Middle East Studies (MES) is an interdisciplinary program that draws on the strengths of faculty from a variety of fields in the humanities and social sciences. The program offers students the opportunity to pursue an in-depth study of the Middle East from a range of disciplinary perspectives while also acquiring language competency in a Middle Eastern language. The major is designed to provide students with a broad overview of the Middle East, along with the opportunity to focus on a particular sub-field, region, or discipline in their elective courses. The program emphasizes critical thinking and analytical skills, as well as the ability to communicate effectively about the Middle East. MES graduates are well-prepared for careers in government, non-profits, international business, law, journalism, and education, as well as for graduate study in a variety of fields.

Concentration name: Anthropology and Sociology; Art and Archaeology; History; History of Religions; Political Science; Women's and Gender Studies
description: The major in Middle East Studies is designed to provide students with a multi-disciplinary grounding in the study of the modern Middle East, while also allowing them to develop a program of study that suits their specific interests. The major is appropriate for students considering graduate school in a variety of disciplines, as well as those who are preparing for careers in government, the private sector, or non-governmental organizations. All majors are required to complete courses in four areas of study: language, core courses, a disciplinary or thematic focus, and a capstone seminar.

The Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology major offers an integrated program of study from the subcellular and molecular level to the level of the whole organism. A student in this program will acquire a strong foundation in the basic sciences of biology, chemistry, physics, and math that will provide the framework to tailor a program to their specific interests.

If you have an interest in biological and behavioral sciences and a desire to help people, a Movement Science major may be for you. The Movement Science program is a Bachelor of Science degree that provides students with a strong scientific foundation to understand the effects of movement on the human body. As a student in this program, you will study the biomechanical and physiological responses to exercise, the psychomotor effects of motor skills, and how they impact human health, and you will learn to apply this knowledge in a wide range of settings. For example, students might study how exercise reduces the risk for chronic diseases, how children acquire motor skills such as walking and reaching, or how to design rehabilitation programs for people with disabilities. The curriculum for Movement Science provides excellent preparation for students interested in a variety of health-related careers including physical therapy, occupational therapy, physician assistant, medicine, and other allied health professions, as well as graduate study in kinesiology.

Concentration name: Composition, Jazz & Contemporary Improvisation, Music & Technology, Music Education, Music Performance, Music Theory, Multidisciplinary Studies
description: Michigan’s School of Music, Theatre & Dance is home to one of the finest music schools in the United States. Its faculty includes internationally renowned performers, composers, scholars, and teachers. Its graduates are leaders in their fields. The bachelor's degree in music is a professional degree, intended to prepare you for a career in music. Several concentration options are available.

Concentration name: ['choral/general music', 'instrumental/general music']
description: The Bachelor of Music in Music Education at the University of Michigan is a professional undergraduate degree program leading to K-12 teacher certification in the state of Michigan. Certification is available in two areas: choral/general music and instrumental/general music. This state-of-the-art program allows students to develop and refine their musicianship while cultivating creative and innovative approaches to teaching in a variety of school and community settings. Students develop a thorough grounding in all aspects of music, including performance, conducting, music theory, and musicology while engaging in extensive coursework in educational psychology and philosophy. Students will have the opportunity to participate in SMTD’s world-class ensembles, lessons, and studios and also experience a variety of hands-on teaching experiences in the field beginning in their first year.
Accreditation status: The School of Music, Theatre & Dance is a member of the National Association of Schools of Music.

Concentration name: Brass, Collaborative Piano, Conducting, Harpsichord, Organ, Percussion, Piano, Strings, Voice, Winds & Brass, Woodwinds
description: The School of Music, Theatre & Dance offers a range of performance degrees through its instrumental and vocal departments. The bachelor of music in performance is a professional degree, providing the highest possible level of training for a career in performance. Studies at the master’s and doctoral levels provide even more intensive preparation for a professional life in music.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

description: The Bachelor of Music in Music Theory is a pre-professional degree designed for students with a strong interest in the academic study of music, with plans to pursue a career in college-level teaching and research. Graduates of our BM program often go on to complete graduate degrees in music theory at some of the finest institutions in North America. They hold positions at a wide variety of colleges, universities, and conservatories across the country and abroad. The curriculum is intended to provide a thorough grounding in the traditional areas of music theory and analysis while exposing students to a variety of new approaches. Students in the program take a variety of advanced theory courses, a course in counterpoint, and a senior thesis. Private studio instruction and participation in ensembles are also required.

Founded in 1880, the University of Michigan School of Music, Theatre & Dance (SMTD) is one of the finest performing arts schools in the United States. The school is home to a world-class faculty of performers, artists, and scholars, and a motivated and talented student body. SMTD offers a wide range of programs in music, theatre, and dance, at the undergraduate and graduate levels. Students have the opportunity to perform in a variety of ensembles and productions, and to work with guest artists from around the world.
Accreditation status: The music programs are accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). The dance program is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Dance (NASD). The theatre program is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST).

description: The Bachelor of Musical Arts (BMA) is a liberal arts-style music degree, allowing students to combine a professional music curriculum with extensive studies in other fields of interest. The BMA program is best suited for students who are musically talented and wish to continue their music studies at a professional level, but also have strong interests in other academic fields. BMA students take a combination of music courses and academic courses, combining the best of what U-M’s School of Music, Theatre & Dance (SMTD) and the College of Literature, Science, and the Arts (LSA) have to offer. BMA students have a home in SMTD, just like all other undergraduate music students; they take music lessons from our esteemed faculty, and they perform in our many ensembles. The required number of music credits are fewer than in the BM program, however, allowing BMA students to choose an LSA minor, to double major in a program from SMTD and LSA, or even pursue a dual degree. BMA students find that this flexibility, combined with the world-class education offered at both SMTD and LSA, leads to incredible careers.
Accreditation status: All programs of the School of Music, Theatre & Dance are accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music, the National Association of Schools of Theatre, and the National Association of Schools of Dance.

description: The Department of Musical Theatre is one of the oldest and most respected programs in the country. Our curriculum is a potent combination of professional training and broad-based academics offered by an outstanding faculty of working artists and scholars. Through a rigorous and focused curriculum of acting, dance, and voice, students develop a synthesis of skills for a successful career in musical theatre. In addition, the department provides an opportunity for students to experience the full scope of professional theatre through its series of mainstage musicals and plays. Numerous student-produced workshops and presentations also enrich the undergraduate experience.

Concentration name: ['Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering', 'Marine Engineering', 'Yacht Design']
description: Naval architects and marine engineers are on the forefront of green energy and the Blue Economy. Students pursuing a degree in Naval Architecture & Marine Engineering (NA&ME) have a passion for the water and a desire to make an impact on the world, whether through the design of autonomous vessels or the construction of offshore wind farms. NA&ME is a field with rich history and an even brighter future in areas such as sustainability, robotics, and national security.
Accreditation status: The Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering undergraduate program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description: The Neuroscience major provides a course of study for students interested in the brain and its function. The nervous system is explored from the subcellular and molecular levels through a systems-level approach to the study of cognitive and behavioral functions. The coursework for the major progresses from introductory to advanced. After the prerequisites are completed, students take core courses that examine the function of the nervous system from different perspectives, as well as several advanced electives to focus their study on an area of interest within the broader field of neuroscience. In their senior year, majors take an advanced seminar course to experience a more in-depth exploration of a sub-discipline in the field.

Concentration name: Fission Systems and Radiation Transport; Materials and Radiation Effects; Radiological Health Engineering; Plasma Science and Fusion Energy; and Security, Safety, and Nonproliferation
description: The undergraduate program in Nuclear Engineering and Radiological Sciences is a challenging and rewarding curriculum for students who are interested in solving some of the world’s biggest problems. Our students are making a difference in the fields of medicine, energy, and national security. Nuclear engineering and radiological sciences is a broad and diverse discipline that includes: producing carbon-free energy through nuclear fission and fusion; providing homeland security through radiation detection and nonproliferation; developing advanced materials for use in extreme radiation environments; creating innovative ways to diagnose and treat diseases like cancer; and contributing to our understanding of the universe through astrophysics and planetary science. The undergraduate curriculum provides students with a strong background in mathematics and physics and a broad education in the five concentration areas of our department: Fission Systems and Radiation Transport; Materials and Radiation Effects; Radiological Health Engineering; Plasma Science and Fusion Energy; and Security, Safety, and Nonproliferation. The program gives students the flexibility to focus their coursework in an area of their choosing while also experiencing the full scope of our field. Students have many opportunities for undergraduate research with our distinguished faculty, and can also gain valuable experience through internships and co-ops with our industrial partners. Our alumni go on to careers in industry, national laboratories, government, and medicine, and they are well prepared for graduate studies in a variety of fields.
Accreditation status: The U-M NERS BSE Program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description: The Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) degree is a four-year program that prepares students to become first-level professional practitioners in a variety of health care settings, as well as for graduate study. Following graduation, you'll be eligible to take the NCLEX-RN examination, the national licensure exam to become a registered nurse (RN).
Accreditation status: The baccalaureate degree program in nursing, master's degree program in nursing, Doctor of Nursing Practice program and post-graduate APRN certificate program at the University of Michigan are accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education, 655 K Street NW, Suite 750, Washington, DC 20001, 202-887-6791.

description: Nutritional sciences students explore the complex and evolving field of human nutrition by critically examining the link between diet, health, and disease. Students learn how essential nutrients affect the body on a cellular, systemic, and whole-body level, how nutrition needs change throughout the lifespan, and how diet can be used to treat and prevent chronic diseases. Our program is a great fit for students who want to become a registered dietitian (RD) or are interested in careers in medicine, dentistry, physical therapy, pharmacy, public health, nursing, or research.
Accreditation status: The Didactic Program in Dietetics (DPD) at the University of Michigan School of Kinesiology is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND) of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics.

description: Organizational Studies (OS) is an interdisciplinary undergraduate major that draws upon the social sciences to explore the nature and workings of organizations and their effect on individuals and society. The program has a special interest in preparing students for careers in social entrepreneurship, human resources, management consulting, social and community service, law, and business. OS provides students with an analytic framework for understanding organizations and gives them the qualitative and quantitative skills to successfully manage, change, and work in organizations. The OS curriculum emphasizes three levels of analysis: the organization and its environment, the organization as a social system, and the individual in the organization.

Concentration name: Sound Engineering
description: The Department of Performing Arts Technology (PAT) at the University of Michigan School of Music, Theatre & Dance is a leader in the education of artists and engineers who are fluent in the creative application of emerging media technologies. A highly interdisciplinary curriculum, which allows students to choose one of two distinct degree paths, is complemented by state-of-the-art facilities and a celebrated faculty of artists, composers, engineers, and researchers. Students in the department come from diverse creative backgrounds and go on to become leaders and innovators in a wide variety of creative industries. Students can choose between two undergraduate degree programs: the Bachelor of Fine Arts in Performing Arts Technology and the Bachelor of Science in Sound Engineering.

The Bachelor of Science in Pharmaceutical Sciences (BSPS) is a science-based undergraduate program that provides a unique interdisciplinary curriculum, drawing from biology, chemistry, math, and medicine to explore the discovery, development, and use of pharmaceuticals. As a BSPS major, you’ll focus on the science behind drug action, development, and delivery. You'll work side-by-side with world-renowned faculty in state-of-the-art facilities, participate in high-impact research experiences, and build a strong foundation in basic and applied pharmaceutical sciences. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in the basic and applied pharmaceutical sciences and excellent preparation for professional school (pharmacy, medicine, dentistry, etc.) or post-graduate study in a wide range of health-related fields. In addition, you’ll be prepared for careers in research, sales, or regulatory affairs in the pharmaceutical industry or in government.

Philosophy is the oldest of the intellectual disciplines and the one that is most general in its concerns. Almost any subject of human inquiry can become the occasion for philosophical reflection. Philosophy explores fundamental questions about the nature of reality, knowledge, and value. Students in philosophy examine the views of major thinkers of the past and present, learn to analyze and evaluate their arguments, and develop and defend their own views on these issues. By studying philosophy, students develop their capacity for critical thinking, careful reasoning, and clear, effective writing and speaking. These skills are of immense value in any field of human endeavor, and U-M philosophy graduates pursue careers in a wide variety of areas, including law, medicine, business, government, and education.

Philosophy majors investigate such abstract questions as: What is the nature of consciousness? What is the best way to live? Is it rational to believe in God? Are there objective truths about the world? Students study the works of major philosophers, past and present, and are encouraged to develop their own philosophical views. They develop their abilities to reason logically, to analyze and evaluate arguments, and to express their own ideas in a clear and persuasive manner. The Philosophy Department offers an honors major, a minor in philosophy, a minor in law and philosophy, and a minor in moral and political philosophy.

Concentration name: Philosophy, Political Science, or Economics
description: The Philosophy, Politics, and Economics (PPE) major is designed for students who seek a broad and rigorous training in the foundations of the social sciences. The major is organized around the conviction that the disciplines of philosophy, political science, and economics have important things to say to each other and that a good training in the social sciences should integrate a student's understanding of these three subjects. To that end, the PPE major has an interdisciplinary structure that requires students to master the analytic tools of the three disciplines and to apply them to a wide range of social problems.

The U-M Physics Department provides a rigorous curriculum in physics, including both coursework and research opportunities, within a liberal arts framework. The department offers several undergraduate degree programs, intended to suit the needs of a variety of students, from those who wish to pursue a career in physics or a related field, to those who simply want a strong quantitative background for a career in fields such as law or medicine. The BS degree program is designed for those students who desire a strong foundation in physics, either for a career in physics or a related technical field, or in preparation for graduate school. The general physics major is intended for students who wish to combine the study of physics with a related field, or with pre-professional requirements. The interdisciplinary programs are intended for students who have a focused interest in an interdisciplinary area.

Concentration name: ['Performance', 'Music Education']
description: The Department of Piano at the University of Michigan School of Music, Theatre & Dance offers a wide array of opportunities for the study of keyboard instruments in an environment that is both nurturing and challenging. Dedicated to providing a comprehensive musical education to talented students from across the country and around the world, the department’s renowned faculty is comprised of artist-teachers equally at home in the studio and on the concert stage. Students at all levels receive a solid grounding in the essentials of keyboard technique and musicianship, while also being encouraged to develop their own artistic personalities. The core of instruction consists of a weekly private lesson with a master teacher. In addition, students have weekly performance classes, and also participate in a variety of small and large ensembles, including the renowned U-M contemporary directions ensemble. Coursework includes a full range of classes in music theory and musicology, as well as a rich curriculum of electives.
Accreditation status: The School of Music, Theatre & Dance is a founding member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM), and has been continuously accredited by that body since 1928.

description: Plants are fundamental to all life on Earth. They provide the food we eat, the oxygen we breathe, and ﬁber for clothing and shelter. Plant biology has direct bearing on many of the critical environmental issues we currently face, such as climate change, conservation biology, and sustainability. Through research, we can address these challenges by improving crop yields, developing biofuels, and discovering new medicines. The Plant Biology major emphasizes the integrative nature of plant science and provides a strong background for graduate study or employment in a variety of jobs in government, academia, or private industry.

The Polish minor offers students interested in Poland an opportunity to combine the study of the Polish language with course work in English on Polish literature, film, and culture. A minimum of four semesters of Polish is required, along with a course on Polish culture taught in English. By fulfilling the requirements for the minor, students will be able to demonstrate at least an intermediate-mid proficiency in Polish in all four skills (speaking, listening, reading, writing). This can be documented by taking a proficiency test. Students will also be able to demonstrate a good knowledge of Polish history and culture, and they will be able to read and analyze literary works in Polish with the help of a dictionary.

Political Science is a broad discipline that seeks to understand politics in all its dimensions. The curriculum is organized around four main fields: American politics, comparative politics, political theory, and world politics. Each field addresses a core set of questions about politics and provides a different lens to understand the political world. Through a wide variety of coursework in these fields, students in the political science major will gain a deeper understanding of political concepts and processes, learn about political systems and behavior in the US and around the world, and engage with enduring questions about justice, power, and the good life. Students will also learn social scientific methods and how to apply them to better understand the political world. By taking political science courses, students will strengthen their ability to think critically, communicate effectively, and engage thoughtfully in civic life.

Political Science is the study of how people gain and use power to make collective decisions in a world of conflicting interests. It examines political behavior in a variety of contexts, including elections, social movements, international relations, and public policy making. The political science major can provide excellent preparation for a career in government, law, business, education, journalism, or public service. Students take a combination of classes in four areas: American politics, comparative politics, political theory, and world politics. U-M also offers a minor in political science and a minor in international security, norms, and cooperation through the Political Science department.

The Sweetland Center for Writing offers a major in Writing for LSA students. The major in Writing provides students with a sustained and theoretically-grounded education in the study and practice of writing in a variety of non-academic genres. Writing majors will develop a greater knowledge of, and sophistication with, written argumentation and language; an understanding of writing as an intellectual and ethical practice; an ability to conduct inquiry-based research, and the rhetorical knowledge to shape writing for a wide range of audiences and purposes.

Concentration name: Research-Focused Emphasis
description: Psychology is the scientific study of the mind, the brain, and human behavior. Psychologists use the scientific method to answer questions about how we think, feel, and act, and then they apply that knowledge to the real world. Psychology at Michigan is uniquely interdisciplinary and research-oriented. Students take courses in six different areas of psychology: behavioral and cognitive neuroscience, clinical, cognitive, developmental, organizational, and social.

Psychology is the scientific study of the mind, brain, and human behavior. Psychologists study everything from the basic workings of the human brain to consciousness, memory, reasoning, and language, to personality and mental health. Students will take courses in a variety of areas, including biopsychology, cognition, developmental psychology, and social psychology. In this major, you can focus your course of study around a particular area of psychology and/or learn how psychological principles are applied in a variety of other fields. You'll complete a combination of introductory and upper-level courses, and will have the option to complete an original research project as a part of an honors thesis. Many students go on to graduate study in the discipline. With a degree in psychology, you’ll also be prepared for a variety of careers in business, law, medicine, human services, and education.

The School of Public Health is consistently ranked among the top schools of public health in the nation and is fully accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH). Students interested in public health can major in Community and Global Public Health (BA) or Public Health Sciences (BA or BS). Both majors focus on health and disease at the population level. Students will gain an understanding of the five core disciplines of public health, which allows them to explore the complex biological, social, economic, and political factors that affect the health of communities and populations worldwide. Students are taught and mentored by faculty who are recognized leaders in their fields, and have access to world-class resources. Experiential learning is an important aspect of a public health education. As a part of the major, students are required to complete an internship with a public health organization. To prepare for their internship and future career, students have a variety of resources available to them, including a public health-specific career fair and one-on-one advising sessions with a career counselor. Our students successfully secure employment across a broad range of settings, including government, non-profit organizations, healthcare, and industry in collaboration with SPH Career Services.
Accreditation status: The School of Public Health is consistently ranked among the top schools of public health in the nation and is fully accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).

description: The Ford School’s Bachelor of Arts in public policy is a liberal arts degree based in the social sciences. As a public policy major, you will learn to understand, analyze, and address a wide range of societal problems, from injustice and inequality to inefficiency and waste. You will build a strong foundation in economics, political science, and sociology. You will learn and apply quantitative and qualitative analytic methods. You will work with diverse communities and organizations on real-world policy challenges. And you will write, speak, and collaborate in ways that build consensus and inspire positive change. The Ford School’s undergraduate curriculum provides you with the skills and knowledge to be an effective and ethical policy analyst, leader, and citizen.

This program is for students who want a deep and broad knowledge of mathematics. It is especially recommended for students who plan to go to graduate school in mathematics. It is also a good choice for any student who has a strong interest in the more theoretical side of mathematics. Students who complete the requirements of this program will earn a Bachelor of Science in Mathematics.

Research Administration is one of the fastest growing professions in the U.S. and supports researchers and institutions where research is conducted. This interdisciplinary program is designed for students interested in working on the administrative side of a research enterprise, including universities, hospitals, private industry, and government. You will build a foundation for understanding the legal, ethical, and financial policies governing research by taking courses in the School of Education, social sciences, natural sciences, and humanities. In the final year of the program, you will synthesize learning across courses and apply it to an authentic problem of practice through a required internship and capstone course.

Concentration name: Mechanical Engineering, Electrical & Computer Engineering, Computer Science
description: Robotics is an interdisciplinary field, and our undergraduate curriculum reflects that. At its core, robotics is the study of embodied intelligent systems. This means students need a strong foundation across a number of technical areas. Our curriculum provides students a unified approach to robotics, framed around three pillars: Sense, Think, Act. It combines a rigorous theoretical foundation with project-based, hands-on learning. We aim to produce students who are not only capable of understanding the existing robotic systems, but who can also design and create the next generation of robotic systems that will benefit society. Students will choose one of three technical concentrations, each of which is composed of four courses (15-16 credits).
Accreditation status: The Robotics undergraduate program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Robotics and Mechatronics Engineering Program Criteria.

Concentration name: French, Italian, Portuguese, or Spanish
description: This major is designed to give students a thorough grounding in the language and literature of two Romance languages (French, Italian, Portuguese, or Spanish). Students should also acquire a good speaking and writing knowledge of the languages and an acquaintance with the culture of the countries in which they are spoken. The program requires 20-21 credits beyond the prerequisite language courses. The Department of Romance Languages and Literatures offers a broad spectrum of courses in language, literature, culture, and linguistics.

The minor in Russian Studies is designed for students who want a broader, interdisciplinary approach to the field than the Russian minor allows. A knowledge of Russian language is necessary for this minor, but students focus less on linguistic and literary study and more on courses in the social sciences and humanities. A total of 18 credits are required for the minor. Students take one language course and two core courses in Russian culture and history. For the remaining nine credits, students choose from a list of electives in political science, history, sociology, film and media studies, Slavic literatures and cultures, and history of art. All coursework for the minor must be passed with a grade of C- or better.

Concentration name: The major offers three submajors: Screenwriting, Production, and Critical Studies. There is also an FTVM Honors Major.
description: Screen Arts & Cultures is a liberal arts course of study that gives students an understanding of the history, theory, and aesthetics of film, television, and other screen media. The major also provides students with the opportunity to engage creatively with screen media by taking courses in screenwriting and production. Majors learn to think critically and to write analytically about the history of screen media, their aesthetic and formal properties, and their social, cultural, and political effects. Students who major in FTVM have gone on to careers in fields such as film and television criticism, arts management, filmmaking, screenwriting, museum curating, teaching, archiving, journalism, public relations, and advertising. The major also prepares students for further academic study in graduate school in film, television, and media studies.

Concentration name: English, mathematics, social studies, or science. Science concentrations include: comprehensive science (biology, chemistry, earth science, and physics), life sciences (biology), and physical sciences (chemistry and physics).
description: In the undergraduate Secondary Teacher Education (Secondary TE) program, you will develop the knowledge and skills necessary to teach a specific subject in grades 6-12. As a Secondary TE student, you will choose to concentrate in one of the following subject areas: English, mathematics, social studies, or science. We offer three science concentrations: comprehensive science (biology, chemistry, earth science, and physics), life sciences (biology), and physical sciences (chemistry and physics). Your major can be in the subject area that you intend to teach, but it is not required. As a student in our program, you will engage in courses and fieldwork that focus on teaching diverse students in a just and equitable way. To ensure you have plenty of practical experience, we will place you in a local classroom during each semester of the program. You’ll be assigned a field instructor to provide one-on-one coaching and support, while an expert classroom teacher will serve as your mentor. During your final semester, you will be immersed in a full-time internship and take on the responsibilities of a classroom teacher.
Accreditation status: The Marsal Family School of Education is a state-approved teacher preparation institution.

description: The Women’s and Gender Studies Department’s minor in Sexuality, Women's, and Gender Studies (SWAG) offers an interdisciplinary course of study that gives students the analytical tools to understand how gender and sexuality shape human societies. Students are introduced to the key concepts in the field; learn about the history of women's and queer social movements; study how gender and sexuality intersect with race, class, and other social identities; and explore these issues in a transnational context. They develop critical thinking skills through the analysis of a wide range of written and visual texts, and they sharpen their oral and written communication skills through class discussions, presentations, and a variety of writing assignments.

Social Theory and Practice (STP) is an interdisciplinary major that asks students to think critically about the problems of modern societies and the paths to a more just and humane social order. Drawing upon social, political, and cultural theory, STP students learn to analyze historical and contemporary institutions and struggles over power and inequality. The major fosters independent research, community-engaged learning, and collaborative action. Through its two required courses and an array of electives in the social sciences and humanities, the major brings a variety of theoretical and practical perspectives to bear on specific problems and social movements. These range from civil rights and environmental justice to poverty, post-colonial liberation, public health, law, and education. Each student chooses a topical concentration that will form the basis of their intellectual interests in the major.

Concentration name: ['Law, Justice, and Social Change', 'Social Work']
description: Sociology is the scientific study of society. We examine how individuals are shaped by their social settings, how social groups are formed and maintained, how and why societies change, and what the consequences of social change are. Major topics of sociological inquiry include social inequality (class, race, and gender), social institutions (the family, the economy, education), and social change (globalization, social movements). The Department of Sociology at the University of Michigan is consistently ranked as one of the best in the world. As a discipline, sociology is excellent training for a wide variety of careers.

Concentration name: Law, Justice, and Social Change, Sociology of Health and Medicine, International Social Change
description: The sociology major is designed to provide students with a deep understanding of the social world. It teaches students to think critically and analytically about social issues and social life. Students develop both quantitative and qualitative research skills and learn to analyze data and interpret research findings. As a sociology major, you’ll take courses covering a variety of topics, including race and ethnicity, gender and sexuality, health and medicine, law, crime and punishment, social class, and the family. In the process, you’ll develop the skills that will enable you to better understand and engage with the world around you.

Concentration name: computer game design, web engineering, or mobile applications
description: Software engineers are concerned with all aspects of software production from the early stages of system specification to maintaining the system after it has gone into use. In this program, students will learn the principles of software engineering and will learn to apply them to the creation of complex software systems. The curriculum has a strong technical focus that is balanced with an emphasis on professional practice. The curriculum has a strong technical focus with a professional practice emphasis. The core curriculum covers the foundations of computer science and software engineering. Students choose electives from topics such as web engineering, mobile application development, computer game design, artificial intelligence, robotics, computer graphics, and information security. Students in this program must choose a concentration from one of these areas: computer game design, web engineering, or mobile applications.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science in Software Engineering program at UM-Dearborn is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description: The Bachelor of Science in Sound Engineering is a rigorous and creative four-year curriculum that prepares students to become leaders in the art and science of sound engineering. The program builds on a strong undergraduate-level foundation of electrical engineering and computer science from the College of Engineering and is combined with the world-class performance and music instruction of the School of Music, Theatre & Dance. A balance of demanding technical course work, practical hands-on experience in our state-of-the-art studios, and a rich all-encompassing music education ensures that our graduates are well-prepared for any number of exciting career paths in the industry. These paths include music recording and production, live sound reinforcement, sound for film and video, sound for the performing arts, sound for mixed media, and hardware or software design.

Concentration name: ['Space Science', 'Space Engineering']
description: Space sciences is the study of space, from our own solar system to distant galaxies. Space engineering is the application of science and engineering to the design, development, and operation of space systems. At U-M, we are one of the only universities to combine both of these fields into a single comprehensive department. From understanding space weather and predicting solar flares to designing satellites and launching rockets, students in the Department of Climate and Space Sciences and Engineering have the opportunity to make an impact on humankind’s most important challenges. The Space Sciences and Engineering (SSE) undergraduate degree program is designed for students who are passionate about the exploration of space and interested in the science of the space environment and the engineering of space systems. The program provides a broad knowledge of the space environment and the fundamentals of spacecraft design, with specialization tracks in either space science or space engineering. After graduation, SSE students find jobs at established aerospace companies and government agencies, at startups that are part of the booming NewSpace economy, and in other high-tech sectors where a strong background in science and engineering is valued. Many students also choose to go on to graduate school.
Accreditation status: The Space Engineering track of the BSE in Space Sciences and Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description: Spanish is spoken on all five continents, is the official language of 21 countries, and is the second most spoken language in the U.S. and in the world in terms of native speakers. The Hispanic world has produced some of the greatest literary figures of all time, and today it accounts for a large part of the world’s art, music, and film production. A knowledge of the Spanish language and Hispanic cultures is essential for any professional in any part of the world, but it is especially so in the U.S., where the Spanish-speaking population has reached over 50 million. The major and minor in Spanish provide students with a solid liberal arts education and with a series of marketable skills that prepare them for success in an increasingly multilingual and multicultural world. The major provides an opportunity for students to study, in-depth and from an interdisciplinary perspective, the language, literatures, and cultures of the Spanish-speaking world. In addition to gaining a high level of proficiency in Spanish, majors acquire important skills in critical reading, thinking, and writing that are applicable to a wide variety of professions. The minor allows students to pursue their interest in Spanish by studying language, linguistics, literature, and culture at an advanced level.

The Sport Management (SM) program is a specialized business degree that prepares students for the global, diverse, and engaging sport industry. Our program has been widely recognized for its rigorous curriculum, renowned faculty, and hands-on learning opportunities since its inception in 1980. Students receive a broad understanding of the business of sport, and are prepared for jobs with professional sport teams, intercollegiate athletics, sport marketing firms, sport media, and an expanding sport-based corporate sector. The undergraduate SM curriculum is comprised of Kinesiology, LSA, and Ross School of Business courses. SM courses are designed to provide students with an understanding of the relationship between sport and society, and the application of specific business principles to the sport industry.

Concentration name: Sport marketing and management, sport policy and analytics, sport and development
description: The undergraduate Sport Management (SM) program in the School of Kinesiology gives students an in-depth understanding of the sport industry. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in the liberal arts and allows for specialization in one of four areas of interest: sport marketing and management, sport policy and analytics, or sport and development. SM students complete coursework covering a variety of topics including economics, communications, sport law, and business. Students also gain hands-on experience by completing a required internship after their junior year. Graduates are positioned to pursue diverse careers with professional sports teams, college athletic departments, corporate sport marketing firms, and sports media.

The statistics major prepares students for careers in business, industry, and government, and for graduate study in statistics and other quantitative fields. The major provides a solid foundation in the fundamentals of statistical theory and practice. The curriculum is flexible and can be tailored to the interests of the individual student through the choice of electives. Statistics is a major offered by the College of LSA and is administered by the Department of Statistics. The Department of Statistics also participates in the Interdepartmental major in Mathematics and Statistics, jointly with the Department of Mathematics. Students completing the major in Statistics earn a Bachelor of Science (BS) or Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree in Statistics.

Supply chain management is the management of a network of interconnected businesses involved in the ultimate provision of product and service packages required by end customers. From forecasting demand and sourcing raw materials to manufacturing products and delivering them to consumers, supply chain managers use a systems approach to manage all the activities involved in physically moving goods.

Concentration name: Directing, Playwriting
description: The Department of Theatre & Drama recognizes that its students are the theatre artists and audiences of the future. The department's goal is to provide its students with an understanding of the intellectual, artistic, and practical aspects of the theatre. To that end, students in the department receive a liberal arts education in the humanities, arts, and sciences combined with pre-professional training in the areas of acting, design and production, directing, playwriting, and theatre studies.

Concentration name: ['Scene Design', 'Lighting Design', 'Costume Design', 'Stage Management']
description: The Department of Theatre & Drama’s BFA in Theatre Design and Production is a rigorous, conservatory-style program that prepares students for careers as professional designers, technicians, and artisans. The curriculum is based on the philosophy that a good designer or technician must understand all aspects of theatre production. All design and production students take a core of required courses covering all areas of design (scenic, costume, and lighting), technology, and management, along with courses in theatre history, dramatic literature, and directing. At the end of their second year, students choose a concentration to study in-depth for the remainder of their time at SMTD. Students graduate with a strong liberal arts education and a portfolio of professional-quality work. Regular portfolio reviews ensure that they are on track to become professional artists and theatre makers.

Urban and Regional Studies is an interdisciplinary liberal arts program focused on the study of cities and metropolitan regions. In this major, students will engage in in-depth studies of urban trends and characteristics, analyze the determinants of those trends, examine their impacts on individuals, social groups, and institutions, and explore the policy issues that arise from them. The program is designed to provide students with a broad and deep understanding of urban affairs through an interdisciplinary mix of courses and a core curriculum that provides a solid foundation of theoretical perspectives and analytical skills.

The Bachelor of Science in Urban Technology is the first undergraduate program of its kind in the United-States. Urban Technology is an interdisciplinary field that connects urban planning and design with technology and data science. The urban technology program addresses a key challenge: the central role of digital technology in cities, and the need for new design and planning approaches that are human-centered, data-informed, and justice-oriented. The program is part of the A. Alfred Taubman College of Architecture and Urban Planning, and features close collaboration with the School of Information, the College of Engineering, and the Ford School of Public Policy. The program prepares students for new kinds of careers at the intersection of cities and technology, such as urban data analyst, civic technologist, smart city strategist, urban product manager, and many others. Taubman College's location in the diverse and complex urban region of Detroit provides a real-world context for student projects and engagement.

The Department of Voice has a long-standing international reputation for producing mature, versatile, and complete artists in opera, concert, and recital performance, and for developing teachers who are leaders in the field. The curriculum is comprehensive, offering an extraordinary breadth and depth of opportunity for performance and scholarship at both the graduate and undergraduate levels. With a superb faculty of artist-teachers, more than 300 voice students, and an energetic calendar of professional-caliber performances, the Department of Voice offers a rich and nurturing environment for gifted and motivated young artists.

This interdisciplinary program, part of the College of Literature, Science, and the Arts, analyzes gender and sexuality as they intersect with race, class, ethnicity, nationality, and other dimensions of social identity. Students use intersectional feminism to address a wide variety of topics including politics, economics, history, law, culture, and medicine. Courses may explore such diverse topics as the social construction of masculinity and femininity; women in the arts; feminist theory; LGBTQ studies; gender and health; the history of sexuality; and gender, race, and class in the workplace. Students learn to think critically, communicate clearly, conduct research, and advocate for social justice.
